name: Kingdom of France (Early Modern)
summary: Valois and Bourbon monarchy that centralised the French state, fought the Italian and Religious wars, and built Europe's leading absolutist power before the Revolution abolished it.

name: French Wars of Religion
summary: Eight civil wars between Catholics and Huguenots that devastated France and ended with Henry IV's conversion and the Edict of Nantes.

name: Reign of Francis I of France
summary: Renaissance king who fought Charles V in Italy, patronised Leonardo and Chambord, and made French the language of administration in 1539.

name: Reign of Henry II of France
summary: Ended the Italian Wars at Cateau-Cambresis in 1559 and died in a tournament accident, leaving power to Catherine de' Medici.

name: Reign of Francis II of France
summary: Teenage king married to Mary Stuart whose brief reign was dominated by the Guise faction.

name: Reign of Charles IX of France
summary: Ruled under his mother Catherine de' Medici; his reign saw the St Bartholomew's Day massacre of Huguenots in 1572.

name: St Bartholomew's Day Massacre
summary: Mass killing of Huguenots in Paris and the provinces beginning 24 August 1572, a turning point in the Wars of Religion.

name: Reign of Henry III of France
summary: Last Valois king, caught between the Catholic League and Henry of Navarre; assassinated in 1589.

name: Reign of Henry IV of France
summary: First Bourbon king; converted to Catholicism, issued the Edict of Nantes in 1598 and rebuilt the kingdom before his assassination.

name: Edict of Nantes
summary: Henry IV's grant of limited toleration and fortified towns to French Protestants, revoked in 1685.

name: Reign of Louis XIII
summary: Reign dominated by Cardinal Richelieu, who broke Huguenot autonomy and entered the Thirty Years' War against the Habsburgs.

name: Reign of Louis XIV
summary: Seventy-two-year reign of the Sun King: Versailles, absolutism, revocation of the Edict of Nantes and near-continuous European war.

name: The Fronde
summary: Series of aristocratic and parlementaire revolts during Louis XIV's minority that hardened his commitment to absolutism.

name: Revocation of the Edict of Nantes
summary: Edict of Fontainebleau outlawed Protestantism and drove several hundred thousand Huguenots into exile.

name: Reign of Louis XV
summary: Long reign marked by regency, the War of the Austrian Succession, and the loss of New France and India in the Seven Years' War.

name: Reign of Louis XVI
summary: Fiscal crisis and the summoning of the Estates-General led to revolution; deposed in 1792 and guillotined in 1793.

name: French Revolution
summary: Collapse of the Ancien Regime: Bastille, Declaration of the Rights of Man, republic, Terror and Directory, ending with Bonaparte's coup.

name: Storming of the Bastille
summary: Parisian crowds seized the royal fortress-prison on 14 July 1789, the symbolic start of the Revolution.

name: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
summary: Foundational statement of natural rights adopted by the National Assembly in August 1789.

name: French First Republic
summary: Republic proclaimed after the fall of the monarchy, passing through Convention, Terror, Directory and Consulate before Napoleon's empire.

name: Reign of Terror
summary: Robespierre and the Committee of Public Safety executed tens of thousands until Thermidor ended the Jacobin dictatorship.

name: French Directory
summary: Five-man executive governing France between the Terror and Bonaparte's Brumaire coup.

name: French Consulate
summary: Napoleon Bonaparte ruled as First Consul, creating the Bank of France, the Concordat and the Civil Code.

name: Napoleonic Code
summary: Civil Code of 1804 that codified French private law and became a model across Europe and Latin America.

name: First French Empire
summary: Napoleon I's empire, dominant over continental Europe until defeat in Russia, Leipzig and finally Waterloo.

name: Reign of Napoleon I
summary: Emperor of the French who remade Europe's map and law before abdicating in 1814; briefly restored in 1815.

name: The Hundred Days
summary: Napoleon's return from Elba, restored rule of about a hundred days, and final defeat at Waterloo.

name: Bourbon Restoration
summary: Constitutional monarchy under Louis XVIII and Charles X, ended by the July Revolution.

name: Reign of Louis XVIII
summary: Restored Bourbon king who accepted the Charter of 1814 and steered a moderate course between ultras and liberals.

name: Reign of Charles X of France
summary: Ultra-royalist king whose July Ordinances provoked the 1830 revolution; began the conquest of Algiers.

name: July Revolution
summary: Three days of Parisian fighting in July 1830 that replaced Charles X with Louis-Philippe.

name: July Monarchy
summary: Bourgeois constitutional monarchy of Louis-Philippe, the 'citizen king', toppled in February 1848.

name: Reign of Louis-Philippe I
summary: Orleanist king of the French whose narrow franchise and refusal of reform ended in the February Revolution.

name: French Second Republic
summary: Republic born of the February Revolution, introduced universal male suffrage, ended by Louis-Napoleon's coup.

name: Second French Empire
summary: Napoleon III's authoritarian then liberal empire: Haussmann's Paris, Crimea, Italy, Mexico, and collapse at Sedan.

name: Reign of Napoleon III
summary: Emperor whose modernising rule ended in capture at Sedan and the fall of the empire.

name: Franco-Prussian War
summary: Prussian-led German victory that destroyed the Second Empire, annexed Alsace-Lorraine and completed German unification.

name: Paris Commune
summary: Radical revolutionary government of Paris from March to May 1871, crushed in the semaine sanglante.

name: French Third Republic
summary: Longest-lived French republic: secular laicite laws, colonial expansion, victory in 1914-18, defeat in 1940.

name: Dreyfus Affair
summary: Wrongful conviction of a Jewish officer for treason that split France over antisemitism, army and republic.

name: French Law on the Separation of Church and State
summary: 1905 law establishing laicite by ending state recognition and funding of religions.

name: Vichy France
summary: Authoritarian French State under Marshal Petain that collaborated with Nazi Germany after the 1940 armistice.

name: Free France
summary: De Gaulle's government-in-exile and its forces, which rallied the empire and the Resistance against Vichy and Germany.

name: Provisional Government of the French Republic
summary: De Gaulle-led government that restored republican legality, nationalised key industries and gave women the vote.

name: French Fourth Republic
summary: Unstable parliamentary republic that rebuilt the economy and began European integration but foundered on Indochina and Algeria.

name: French Fifth Republic
summary: De Gaulle's semi-presidential republic, France's current constitutional order since 1958.

name: Presidency of Charles de Gaulle
summary: Founding president of the Fifth Republic: Algerian independence, nuclear force de frappe, NATO withdrawal, and resignation after 1968.

name: May 1968 in France
summary: Student revolt and general strike of ten million workers that shook de Gaulle's government.

name: Presidency of Georges Pompidou
summary: Gaullist president who oversaw industrial modernisation and accepted British entry into the EEC; died in office.

name: Presidency of Valery Giscard d'Estaing
summary: Centrist president who liberalised social law, legalised abortion and helped create the European Monetary System.

name: Presidency of Francois Mitterrand
summary: First Socialist president of the Fifth Republic; nationalisations then austerity, abolition of the death penalty, Maastricht.

name: Presidency of Jacques Chirac
summary: Gaullist president who ended conscription, adopted the euro and opposed the 2003 Iraq war.

name: Presidency of Nicolas Sarkozy
summary: Presidency marked by the 2008 financial crisis, NATO reintegration and the Libya intervention.

name: Presidency of Francois Hollande
summary: Socialist president who legalised same-sex marriage and led France through the 2015 terror attacks and COP21.

name: Presidency of Emmanuel Macron
summary: Centrist president elected 2017 and re-elected 2022, facing gilets jaunes protests, COVID-19 and pension reform.

name: French Colonial Empire
summary: Two successive empires spanning the Americas, Africa, Indochina and the Pacific, largely dissolved between 1954 and 1962.

name: Holy Roman Empire (Early Modern)
summary: Loose confederation of hundreds of German states under an elected emperor, dissolved by Napoleon in 1806.

name: Protestant Reformation
summary: Luther's challenge to Rome split Western Christianity and reshaped European politics, education and warfare.

name: Peace of Augsburg
summary: Settlement letting each German prince choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for his territory, cuius regio eius religio.

name: Thirty Years' War
summary: Religious and dynastic war fought largely in Germany that killed a large share of its population and ended Habsburg hegemony.

name: Defenestration of Prague
summary: Bohemian Protestants threw imperial regents from a castle window, triggering the Thirty Years' War.

name: Peace of Westphalia
summary: Treaties of Munster and Osnabruck that ended the Thirty Years' War and framed the modern system of sovereign states.

name: Brandenburg-Prussia
summary: Hohenzollern union of Brandenburg and Prussia built into a military-bureaucratic state by the Great Elector.

name: Kingdom of Prussia
summary: Hohenzollern kingdom that rose to great-power status, led German unification and dominated the German Empire.

name: Reign of Frederick the Great
summary: Frederick II seized Silesia, survived the Seven Years' War and made Prussia a great power while patronising the Enlightenment.

name: Silesian Wars
summary: Three wars in which Prussia took and kept Silesia from Habsburg Austria.

name: Confederation of the Rhine
summary: Napoleonic client league of German states whose creation ended the Holy Roman Empire.

name: German Confederation
summary: Loose association of 39 German states created at Vienna under Austrian presidency, dissolved after the 1866 war.

name: Zollverein
summary: Prussian-led customs union that economically integrated Germany ahead of political unification.

name: Frankfurt Parliament
summary: First freely elected all-German assembly; drafted a liberal constitution that Prussia's king refused.

name: Austro-Prussian War
summary: Seven Weeks' War in which Prussia's victory at Koniggratz excluded Austria from Germany.

name: North German Confederation
summary: Prussian-dominated federal state that became the framework for the German Empire.

name: German Unification of 1871
summary: Proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles on 18 January 1871, completing Bismarck's unification by war and diplomacy.

name: German Empire
summary: Federal Hohenzollern empire, Europe's leading industrial and military power, which collapsed in revolution in November 1918.

name: Reign of Wilhelm I
summary: First German emperor, whose reign under Bismarck saw unification, the Kulturkampf and the first welfare state.

name: Bismarck's Chancellorship
summary: Otto von Bismarck governed the new empire, building alliances abroad and social insurance and anti-socialist laws at home.

name: Year of the Three Emperors
summary: Wilhelm I, Friedrich III and Wilhelm II all reigned in 1888; Friedrich III ruled only 99 days.

name: Reign of Wilhelm II
summary: Last German emperor: naval race, Weltpolitik, the First World War and abdication in November 1918.

name: German Revolution of 1918-19
summary: Naval mutiny and workers' councils toppled the monarchy and produced the Weimar Republic amid failed communist risings.

name: Weimar Republic
summary: Germany's first democracy: hyperinflation, Ruhr occupation, Weimar culture, then depression and Nazi takeover.

name: German Hyperinflation of 1923
summary: Currency collapse that destroyed savings and discredited the young republic before the Rentenmark stabilisation.

name: Beer Hall Putsch
summary: Hitler's failed Munich coup, after which he wrote Mein Kampf in prison.

name: Nazi Germany
summary: Hitler's totalitarian Third Reich: rearmament, persecution, conquest of Europe, the Holocaust and total defeat.

name: Hitler's Rule of Germany
summary: Adolf Hitler as chancellor and Fuhrer held dictatorial power from 1933 until his suicide in Berlin in April 1945.

name: Nuremberg Laws
summary: Racial laws stripping German Jews of citizenship and criminalising intermarriage.

name: Anschluss
summary: German annexation of Austria in March 1938, endorsed by a rigged plebiscite.

name: Kristallnacht
summary: November 1938 pogrom that destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses across Germany and Austria.

name: Munich Agreement
summary: Britain, France, Germany and Italy ceded the Sudetenland to Hitler, the high point of appeasement.

name: Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact
summary: Nazi-Soviet non-aggression pact with secret protocols dividing Eastern Europe, signed days before war.

name: Allied Occupation of Germany
summary: Four-power division of Germany, denazification, the Nuremberg trials and the Berlin airlift, ending with two German states.

name: Nuremberg Trials
summary: International Military Tribunal that tried surviving Nazi leaders and established modern precedents for crimes against humanity.

name: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
summary: Soviet closure of land routes to West Berlin, defeated by an eleven-month Western airlift.

name: Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany)
summary: Democratic western state founded in 1949; Wirtschaftswunder, NATO membership and Ostpolitik until reunification.

name: German Democratic Republic (East Germany)
summary: Communist state in the Soviet zone, ruled by the SED, dissolved when it acceded to the Federal Republic in 1990.

name: East German Uprising of 1953
summary: Workers' strikes and protests on 17 June 1953 crushed by Soviet tanks.

name: Berlin Wall
summary: Fortified barrier sealing West Berlin from 1961, the Cold War's central symbol, opened on 9 November 1989.

name: Chancellorship of Konrad Adenauer
summary: First West German chancellor: Western integration, NATO entry, reconciliation with France and Israel.

name: Chancellorship of Ludwig Erhard
summary: Architect of the social market economy who succeeded Adenauer as chancellor.

name: Chancellorship of Kurt Georg Kiesinger
summary: Led the first grand coalition of CDU and SPD.

name: Chancellorship of Willy Brandt
summary: Social Democrat who pursued Ostpolitik, knelt at the Warsaw Ghetto memorial and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Chancellorship of Helmut Schmidt
summary: Managed oil shocks, the Red Army Faction's German Autumn and NATO's missile deployment.

name: Chancellorship of Helmut Kohl
summary: Longest-serving postwar chancellor; delivered reunification in 1990 and pushed the euro at Maastricht.

name: German Reunification
summary: On 3 October 1990 the GDR acceded to the Federal Republic under the Two Plus Four Treaty.

name: Federal Republic of Germany
summary: Reunified democratic Germany, the European Union's largest economy, with its capital returned to Berlin.

name: Chancellorship of Gerhard Schroder
summary: SPD-Green government: Kosovo deployment, Agenda 2010 labour reforms, refusal to join the Iraq war.

name: Chancellorship of Angela Merkel
summary: First woman chancellor; steered Germany through the eurozone crisis, the 2015 refugee influx and COVID-19.

name: Chancellorship of Olaf Scholz
summary: Led a three-party coalition through the Zeitenwende response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine and an energy crisis.

name: Chancellorship of Friedrich Merz
summary: CDU chancellor from 2025 heading a coalition with the Social Democrats.

name: Italian Wars
summary: Six decades of conflict over Italy between France, Spain and the Habsburgs, ending in Spanish dominance of the peninsula.

name: Republic of Venice (late)
summary: Declining maritime republic that lost Cyprus and Crete to the Ottomans and was extinguished by Napoleon in 1797.

name: Republic of Genoa (late)
summary: Banking and maritime republic tied to Habsburg Spain, annexed to Napoleon's Ligurian Republic.

name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
summary: Medici then Habsburg-Lorraine state centred on Florence, absorbed into unified Italy.

name: Papal States (Early Modern to 1870)
summary: Territorial dominion of the popes across central Italy, reduced in 1860 and ended by the capture of Rome in 1870.

name: Spanish then Austrian Milan
summary: Duchy of Milan ruled by Habsburg Spain and then Austria before the Napoleonic conquest.

name: Kingdom of Naples (Early Modern)
summary: Spanish then Austrian then Bourbon kingdom of southern Italy, merged into the Two Sicilies in 1816.

name: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
summary: Bourbon kingdom of southern Italy and Sicily, conquered by Garibaldi's volunteers in 1860.

name: Kingdom of Sardinia
summary: Savoyard state based in Piedmont that led the Risorgimento and became the Kingdom of Italy.

name: Risorgimento
summary: Movement of ideas, wars and diplomacy that unified Italy under the House of Savoy.

name: First Italian War of Independence
summary: Piedmontese and revolutionary attempt to expel Austria from northern Italy, defeated at Custoza and Novara.

name: Roman Republic of 1849
summary: Short-lived republic led by Mazzini and defended by Garibaldi until French troops restored the Pope.

name: Second Italian War of Independence
summary: Franco-Piedmontese victory over Austria at Magenta and Solferino won Lombardy for Piedmont.

name: Expedition of the Thousand
summary: Garibaldi's volunteers conquered Sicily and Naples and handed the south to Victor Emmanuel II.

name: Kingdom of Italy
summary: Unified Italian monarchy proclaimed in 1861, which annexed Venetia and Rome, fought both world wars and fell to fascism.

name: Reign of Victor Emmanuel II
summary: First king of united Italy, who annexed Venetia in 1866 and Rome in 1870.

name: Third Italian War of Independence
summary: Italy's war alongside Prussia against Austria, which gained Venetia despite defeats at Custoza and Lissa.

name: Capture of Rome
summary: Italian troops breached Porta Pia on 20 September 1870, ending papal temporal rule and completing unification.

name: Reign of Umberto I
summary: King during colonial expansion in Eritrea and the defeat at Adwa; assassinated by an anarchist in 1900.

name: Reign of Victor Emmanuel III
summary: King who took Italy into the First World War, appointed Mussolini, dismissed him in 1943 and abdicated in 1946.

name: Italo-Turkish War
summary: Italian conquest of Libya and the Dodecanese from the Ottomans.

name: March on Rome
summary: Fascist mobilisation that led the king to appoint Mussolini prime minister in October 1922.

name: Fascist Italy
summary: Mussolini's one-party regime: Lateran Pacts, Ethiopian conquest, Axis alliance and wartime collapse.

name: Lateran Treaty
summary: Agreement creating Vatican City and settling the Roman Question between Italy and the papacy.

name: Vatican City
summary: Sovereign city-state created in 1929 as the seat of the papacy, the world's smallest state.

name: Italian Social Republic
summary: German-backed Salo Republic under Mussolini in northern Italy, fought by the partisan Resistance.

name: Italian Republic
summary: Republic established by the 1946 referendum, a founding member of NATO and the European communities.

name: Years of Lead
summary: Two decades of left- and right-wing terrorism in Italy, including the Red Brigades' murder of Aldo Moro.

name: Republic of San Marino
summary: Ancient micro-republic in the Apennines that preserved independence through Italian unification.

name: Principality of Monaco
summary: Grimaldi principality on the Riviera whose sovereignty was confirmed in 1861 under French protection.

name: Habsburg Spain
summary: Spain under the Austrias, ruling a global empire from the Americas to the Philippines before dynastic extinction in 1700.

name: Spanish Empire
summary: Global empire of the Americas, Philippines and Pacific, dissolved by Latin American independence and 1898.

name: Reign of Charles V
summary: Ruled Spain, the Netherlands, Naples and the Holy Roman Empire; faced Luther and the Ottomans before abdicating.

name: Reign of Philip II of Spain
summary: Height of Spanish power: Lepanto, annexation of Portugal, the Dutch Revolt and the Armada's failure.

name: Spanish Armada
summary: Philip II's invasion fleet against England, scattered by battle and storms.

name: Reign of Philip III of Spain
summary: Reign of truce with the Dutch and the expulsion of the Moriscos.

name: Reign of Philip IV of Spain
summary: Golden-age culture amid decline: loss of the Dutch and Portugal, Catalan revolt and defeat by France.

name: Reign of Charles II of Spain
summary: Last Habsburg king of Spain, childless, whose death triggered the War of the Spanish Succession.

name: War of the Spanish Succession
summary: European war over the Spanish throne that installed the Bourbons and ceded Gibraltar and the Netherlands.

name: Bourbon Spain
summary: Reforming Bourbon monarchy that centralised administration and reorganised the American empire.

name: Reign of Charles III of Spain
summary: Enlightened absolutist who reformed the empire, expelled the Jesuits and modernised Madrid.

name: Peninsular War
summary: Spanish, Portuguese and British resistance to Napoleon's occupation of Iberia, a decisive drain on the French empire.

name: Constitution of Cadiz
summary: Liberal constitution of 1812 that inspired constitutionalism across Spain and Latin America.

name: Carlist Wars
summary: Three dynastic civil wars between supporters of Don Carlos and the liberal monarchy of Isabella II.

name: Reign of Isabella II of Spain
summary: Turbulent reign of civil war and pronunciamientos, ended by the Glorious Revolution of 1868.

name: First Spanish Republic
summary: Short-lived federal republic with four presidents in eleven months, ended by a military coup.

name: Bourbon Restoration in Spain
summary: Restored monarchy under Alfonso XII and Alfonso XIII with alternating parties, the 1898 disaster and Rivera's dictatorship.

name: Spanish-American War
summary: War that stripped Spain of Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines, the 'Disaster of 98'.

name: Dictatorship of Primo de Rivera
summary: Military dictatorship under Alfonso XIII that modernised infrastructure but collapsed in the Depression.

name: Second Spanish Republic
summary: Democratic republic of land reform, regional autonomy and polarisation, destroyed by the Civil War.

name: Spanish Civil War
summary: Nationalist rebels under Franco, aided by Germany and Italy, defeated the Republic, aided by the USSR and volunteers.

name: Francoist Spain
summary: Franco's authoritarian regime: repression, autarky then technocratic growth, ending with his death in 1975.

name: Spanish Transition to Democracy
summary: Dismantling of Francoism under Juan Carlos I and Adolfo Suarez, producing the 1978 constitution.

name: Kingdom of Spain
summary: Parliamentary monarchy since Franco's death, a member of the EU since 1986 and NATO since 1982.

name: Reign of Juan Carlos I
summary: King who oversaw the democratic transition and faced down the 1981 coup attempt; abdicated in 2014.

name: Reign of Felipe VI
summary: King since 2014, whose reign has confronted the Catalan independence crisis of 2017.

name: Catalan Independence Crisis
summary: Unauthorised referendum and unilateral declaration in Catalonia met by direct rule from Madrid.

name: Portuguese Empire
summary: First and longest-lived European seaborne empire, from Ceuta and Goa to Brazil, Angola and Macau.

name: Iberian Union
summary: Sixty years in which Habsburg kings of Spain also ruled Portugal and its empire.

name: Portuguese Restoration War
summary: Revolt that installed the House of Braganza and won recognition of Portuguese independence from Spain.

name: House of Braganza
summary: Dynasty that ruled Portugal and later Brazil until the republican revolution of 1910.

name: Lisbon Earthquake
summary: Earthquake, tsunami and fire that destroyed Lisbon and prompted Pombal's rebuilding and Enlightenment debate.

name: Portuguese Republican Revolution
summary: Lisbon rising that deposed Manuel II and established the First Portuguese Republic.

name: First Portuguese Republic
summary: Unstable republic with dozens of governments, ended by the 28 May military coup.

name: Estado Novo (Portugal)
summary: Salazar's corporatist dictatorship, which clung to the African colonies until the Carnation Revolution.

name: Portuguese Colonial War
summary: Thirteen-year war against independence movements in Angola, Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau that broke the Estado Novo.

name: Carnation Revolution
summary: Bloodless captains' coup of 25 April 1974 that ended dictatorship and led to decolonisation.

name: Portuguese Republic
summary: Democratic republic under the 1976 constitution, an EU member since 1986 and euro founder.

name: Dutch Revolt
summary: Eighty Years' War in which the northern Netherlands won independence from Habsburg Spain.

name: Union of Utrecht
summary: Alliance of northern provinces that became the constitutional basis of the Dutch Republic.

name: Dutch Republic
summary: Republic of the Seven United Provinces: a commercial, naval and financial superpower of the 17th century.

name: Dutch Golden Age
summary: Era of Dutch commercial primacy, Rembrandt and Vermeer, Spinoza, and global trading empire.

name: Dutch East India Company
summary: Chartered company with sovereign powers that dominated Asian trade and founded Batavia and the Cape.

name: Dutch West India Company
summary: Chartered company that ran Dutch Brazil, New Netherland and the Atlantic slave trade.

name: Disaster Year of 1672
summary: French, English and German attack that nearly destroyed the Republic and brought William III to power.

name: Batavian Republic
summary: French-sponsored revolutionary republic that replaced the Dutch Republic.

name: Kingdom of Holland
summary: Napoleonic kingdom under Louis Bonaparte, annexed to France in 1810.

name: United Kingdom of the Netherlands
summary: Congress of Vienna state joining the Dutch and Belgian provinces under William I, split by Belgian independence.

name: Kingdom of the Netherlands
summary: Constitutional monarchy under the House of Orange-Nassau, a founding member of NATO and the European communities.

name: Reign of William I of the Netherlands
summary: First Dutch king; lost Belgium in 1830-39 and abdicated in 1840.

name: Dutch Constitutional Reform of 1848
summary: Thorbecke's revision created ministerial responsibility and parliamentary government.

name: Reign of Queen Wilhelmina
summary: Queen through both world wars who led resistance broadcasts from London exile.

name: Dutch Hunger Winter
summary: Famine in German-occupied western Netherlands that killed some 20,000 people.

name: Reign of Queen Juliana
summary: Queen during Indonesian independence, the 1953 North Sea flood and postwar reconstruction.

name: Reign of Queen Beatrix
summary: Queen for 33 years, abdicating in favour of her son in 2013.

name: Reign of King Willem-Alexander
summary: Dutch king since 2013.

name: Spanish Netherlands
summary: Habsburg Spanish provinces of the southern Low Countries, roughly modern Belgium and Luxembourg.

name: Austrian Netherlands
summary: Habsburg Austrian rule over the southern Low Countries, disrupted by the Brabant Revolution and French annexation.

name: Belgian Revolution
summary: Brussels rising against Dutch rule that created an independent, neutral Belgium recognised in 1839.

name: Kingdom of Belgium
summary: Constitutional monarchy independent since 1830, twice invaded by Germany, now a federal state and EU seat.

name: Reign of Leopold I of Belgium
summary: First king of the Belgians, who secured recognition and neutrality for the new state.

name: Reign of Leopold II of Belgium
summary: King who ran the Congo Free State as personal property, causing mass death, and industrialised Belgium.

name: Reign of Albert I of Belgium
summary: Knight-king who led Belgian resistance to the German invasion of 1914.

name: Reign of Leopold III of Belgium
summary: Surrendered in 1940 and remained in occupied Belgium; abdicated after the postwar Royal Question.

name: Reign of King Baudouin
summary: King during Congolese independence and the federalisation of Belgium.

name: Federalisation of Belgium
summary: Series of state reforms that turned unitary Belgium into a federation of language communities and regions.

name: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
summary: Grand duchy created at Vienna, fully independent since 1839-1890, a founding member of the European communities.

name: Old Swiss Confederacy
summary: League of thirteen cantons whose independence from the Empire was recognised in 1648 and which pioneered armed neutrality.

name: Swiss Reformation
summary: Zwingli in Zurich and later Calvin in Geneva made Switzerland a centre of Reformed Protestantism.

name: Helvetic Republic
summary: French-imposed centralised republic that replaced the cantonal confederacy.

name: Restored Swiss Confederation
summary: Confederation of 22 cantons whose perpetual neutrality was guaranteed at the Congress of Vienna.

name: Sonderbund War
summary: Brief civil war in which federal forces defeated a league of Catholic cantons, clearing the way for the 1848 constitution.

name: Swiss Confederation
summary: Federal state created by the 1848 constitution, neutral, directly democratic and home to many international bodies.

name: Swiss Women's Suffrage
summary: Federal referendum granting women the vote, among the last in Europe.

name: Principality of Liechtenstein
summary: Alpine principality created in 1719, sovereign since 1806 and closely tied to Switzerland.

name: Principality of Andorra
summary: Pyrenean co-principality under the Spanish bishop of Urgell and the French head of state; parliamentary since 1993.

name: Kalmar Union (late)
summary: Dynastic union of Denmark, Norway and Sweden that broke up when Sweden seceded under Gustav Vasa.

name: Swedish War of Liberation
summary: Rising led by Gustav Vasa after the Stockholm Bloodbath that ended Danish rule and the Kalmar Union.

name: House of Vasa
summary: Dynasty that made Sweden Protestant, hereditary and a great power in the Baltic.

name: Reign of Gustav I Vasa
summary: Founder of modern Sweden: broke with Denmark and Rome, created a hereditary Lutheran monarchy.

name: Reign of Gustavus Adolphus
summary: Warrior king who reformed the army and intervened decisively in the Thirty Years' War; killed at Lutzen.

name: Swedish Empire
summary: Stormaktstiden, when Sweden controlled much of the Baltic littoral until defeat in the Great Northern War.

name: Reign of Queen Christina
summary: Learned queen who ended the Thirty Years' War, then abdicated and converted to Catholicism.

name: Great Northern War
summary: Coalition war that destroyed Sweden's Baltic empire and established Russia as a great power.

name: Reign of Charles XII of Sweden
summary: Warrior king whose victories ended at Poltava in 1709; killed besieging Fredriksten.

name: Swedish Age of Liberty
summary: Period of parliamentary dominance by the Riksdag over a weakened crown, ended by Gustav III's coup.

name: Reign of Gustav III of Sweden
summary: Enlightened absolutist who restored royal power by coup and was assassinated at a masked ball.

name: House of Bernadotte
summary: Dynasty founded by Napoleon's marshal Jean Bernadotte, still reigning in Sweden.

name: Union of Sweden and Norway
summary: Personal union imposed after Denmark ceded Norway, dissolved peacefully in 1905.

name: Kingdom of Sweden
summary: Continuous Swedish state since 1523, neutral through both world wars, an EU member from 1995 and NATO from 2024.

name: Reign of Gustaf V of Sweden
summary: Longest-reigning modern Swedish king, on the throne through both world wars and the rise of social democracy.

name: Reign of Carl XVI Gustaf
summary: Swedish king since 1973 under the 1974 instrument of government that stripped royal political power.

name: Swedish Accession to NATO
summary: Sweden abandoned two centuries of non-alignment and joined NATO in March 2024 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

name: Denmark-Norway
summary: Oldenburg composite monarchy of Denmark, Norway, Iceland and the North Atlantic islands, split at Kiel in 1814.

name: Danish Absolutism
summary: Hereditary absolute monarchy codified in the Lex Regia of 1665, ended by the 1849 constitution.

name: Treaty of Kiel
summary: Denmark ceded Norway to Sweden after backing Napoleon, keeping Iceland, Greenland and the Faroes.

name: Kingdom of Denmark
summary: Europe's oldest continuous monarchy, constitutional since 1849, occupied 1940-45, an EU member since 1973.

name: Danish June Constitution
summary: Constitution ending absolutism and creating a bicameral parliament.

name: First Schleswig War
summary: Danish victory over Schleswig-Holstein German nationalists and their German allies.

name: Second Schleswig War
summary: Prussian-Austrian defeat of Denmark, which lost Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg.

name: Reign of Christian X of Denmark
summary: King during the Easter Crisis, Icelandic separation and the German occupation, when he became a symbol of resistance.

name: Reign of Margrethe II
summary: Denmark's first queen regnant in modern times, who abdicated in 2024 after 52 years.

name: Reign of Frederik X
summary: King of Denmark since January 2024.

name: Greenland Home Rule and Self-Government
summary: Greenland gained home rule in 1979, extended to self-government in 2009 within the Danish realm.

name: Kingdom of Norway
summary: Independent constitutional monarchy since the 1905 dissolution of the union with Sweden; oil wealth since the 1970s.

name: Norwegian Constitution of 1814
summary: Eidsvoll assembly's liberal constitution, still in force and celebrated on 17 May.

name: Dissolution of the Union with Sweden
summary: Peaceful separation confirmed by referendum, with Prince Carl of Denmark crowned Haakon VII.

name: Reign of Haakon VII
summary: First king of independent Norway, who refused to legitimise the German occupation and led resistance from London.

name: German Occupation of Norway
summary: Five years of German rule under Quisling's collaborationist administration.

name: Reign of Harald V
summary: King of Norway since 1991.

name: Icelandic Sovereignty and Republic
summary: Iceland became a sovereign kingdom in personal union with Denmark in 1918 and a republic in 1944.

name: Republic of Iceland
summary: Republic declared in 1944, NATO founder, hit hard by the 2008 banking collapse.

name: Cod Wars
summary: Disputes with Britain over fishing limits that Iceland won, extending its zone to 200 miles.

name: Grand Duchy of Finland
summary: Autonomous Russian grand duchy where Finnish national identity and institutions took shape.

name: Finnish Declaration of Independence
summary: Finland declared independence from revolutionary Russia on 6 December 1917.

name: Finnish Civil War
summary: Whites under Mannerheim defeated the Reds in a brief, bloody conflict after independence.

name: Republic of Finland
summary: Nordic republic that preserved independence against the USSR, joined the EU in 1995 and NATO in 2023.

name: Winter War
summary: Soviet invasion resisted fiercely by Finland, which ceded Karelia in the Moscow Peace.

name: Continuation War
summary: Finland's co-belligerent war alongside Germany, ended by armistice and territorial loss.

name: Finlandization
summary: Cold War policy of neutrality and accommodation with the USSR while remaining a Western democracy.

name: Finnish Accession to NATO
summary: Finland joined NATO in April 2023, ending decades of military non-alignment.

name: Swedish and Polish Livonia
summary: Partition of the Livonian Order's lands among Sweden, Poland-Lithuania and Denmark after the Livonian War.

name: Baltic Provinces of the Russian Empire
summary: Estonia, Livonia and Courland under Russian rule with Baltic German elites, until 1918 independence.

name: Republic of Estonia (first period)
summary: Independent Estonia after the War of Independence against Soviet Russia and the Baltic Germans, annexed by the USSR in 1940.

name: Republic of Latvia (first period)
summary: Independent Latvia between the wars, ended by Soviet annexation under the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact.

name: Republic of Lithuania (first period)
summary: Interwar Lithuania, which lost Vilnius to Poland and was annexed by the USSR in 1940.

name: Soviet Annexation of the Baltic States
summary: Forced incorporation of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania into the USSR, followed by deportations.

name: Singing Revolution
summary: Mass non-violent movement, including the 1989 Baltic Way human chain, that restored Baltic independence.

name: Republic of Estonia
summary: Baltic republic that restored independence in 1991 and joined the EU and NATO in 2004; a digital-government pioneer.

name: Republic of Latvia
summary: Baltic republic independent again from 1991, in the EU and NATO since 2004 and the euro since 2014.

name: Republic of Lithuania
summary: First Soviet republic to declare independence, in March 1990; EU and NATO member since 2004.

name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
summary: Elective monarchy and noble republic, once Europe's largest state, paralysed by the liberum veto and destroyed by partition.

name: Union of Lublin
summary: Treaty creating a single Commonwealth with one monarch, diet and currency.

name: The Deluge
summary: Swedish and Russian invasions that devastated Poland-Lithuania and began its long decline.

name: Battle of Vienna
summary: Polish, Imperial and German relief army under Jan III Sobieski broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna.

name: Constitution of 3 May 1791
summary: Europe's first modern codified constitution, an attempt at reform that provoked partition.

name: First Partition of Poland
summary: Russia, Prussia and Austria seized about a third of Commonwealth territory.

name: Second Partition of Poland
summary: Russia and Prussia took further large territories after the war in defence of the 1791 constitution.

name: Kosciuszko Uprising
summary: National insurrection led by Tadeusz Kosciuszko, defeated by Russia and Prussia.

name: Third Partition of Poland
summary: Final partition erased Poland-Lithuania from the map for 123 years.

name: Duchy of Warsaw
summary: Napoleonic Polish state that revived hopes of independence and supplied troops for the Grande Armee.

name: Kingdom of Poland (Congress Poland)
summary: Russian-ruled Polish kingdom whose autonomy was stripped after the 1830 and 1863 uprisings.

name: November Uprising
summary: Polish revolt against Russian rule, crushed with the loss of the kingdom's army and constitution.

name: January Uprising
summary: Largest Polish insurrection against Russia, followed by Russification and the abolition of serfdom.

name: Second Polish Republic
summary: Poland restored in 1918, victorious over Soviet Russia in 1920, ruled after 1926 by Pilsudski's Sanacja, destroyed in 1939.

name: Polish-Soviet War
summary: War ended by Poland's victory at the Vistula in 1920 and the Treaty of Riga.

name: Invasion of Poland
summary: German attack on 1 September and Soviet attack on 17 September partitioned Poland and began the Second World War.

name: General Government
summary: German occupation regime in central Poland, site of mass murder including the extermination camps.

name: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
summary: Jewish armed revolt against deportations to Treblinka, crushed with the ghetto's destruction.

name: Warsaw Uprising
summary: Home Army rising for 63 days, defeated while Soviet forces halted; Warsaw was razed in reprisal.

name: Polish People's Republic
summary: Communist Poland, shaken by 1956, 1968, 1970 and 1980 protests and by martial law in 1981.

name: Solidarity
summary: Independent trade union born in Gdansk under Lech Walesa that led the peaceful end of communist rule.

name: Polish Martial Law
summary: General Jaruzelski's crackdown that interned Solidarity leaders and suspended civil liberties.

name: Polish Round Table Talks
summary: Negotiations that produced semi-free elections and the first non-communist government in the bloc.

name: Third Polish Republic
summary: Democratic Poland since 1989, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004.

name: Habsburg Monarchy
summary: Composite realm of Austria, Bohemia and Hungary that anchored Catholic Europe and fought the Ottomans and Prussia.

name: Reign of Maria Theresa
summary: Only female ruler of the Habsburg lands: survived the succession war, lost Silesia and reformed the state.

name: Reign of Joseph II
summary: Radical enlightened absolutist who abolished serfdom and issued the Patent of Toleration.

name: Austrian Empire
summary: Empire proclaimed by Francis II in response to Napoleon, dominant in the German Confederation until 1866.

name: Metternich Era
summary: Conservative order of censorship, congresses and repression of nationalism directed from Vienna.

name: Reign of Franz Joseph I
summary: Sixty-eight-year reign spanning 1848, the Compromise of 1867, and the outbreak of the First World War.

name: Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867
summary: Agreement creating the Dual Monarchy with separate Austrian and Hungarian governments under one emperor-king.

name: Austro-Hungarian Empire
summary: Multinational dual monarchy of eleven major nationalities that dissolved in defeat in 1918.

name: Austro-Hungarian Annexation of Bosnia
summary: Formal annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, inflaming Serbian nationalism and Russian rivalry.

name: Reign of Charles I of Austria
summary: Last Habsburg emperor, whose peace efforts failed and whose empire dissolved in 1918.

name: First Austrian Republic
summary: Rump Austrian republic of political violence between Social Democrats and Christian Socials.

name: Federal State of Austria
summary: Dollfuss and Schuschnigg's clerical-authoritarian state, ended by German annexation.

name: Allied Occupation of Austria
summary: Four-power occupation ended by the State Treaty, which restored sovereignty on condition of neutrality.

name: Republic of Austria
summary: Neutral democratic republic, sovereign from 1955 and an EU member since 1995.

name: Kingdom of Hungary under the Habsburgs
summary: Hungarian crown held by the Habsburgs, partly Ottoman-occupied until 1699 and repeatedly in revolt.

name: Ottoman Hungary
summary: Central Hungary under Ottoman rule after Mohacs, recovered by the Habsburgs at Karlowitz.

name: Rakoczi's War of Independence
summary: Large anti-Habsburg revolt led by Francis II Rakoczi, ended by the Peace of Szatmar.

name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
summary: Kossuth's national revolution and war of independence, defeated by Austrian and Russian armies.

name: Hungarian Soviet Republic
summary: Bela Kun's 133-day communist regime, overthrown after Romanian invasion.

name: Treaty of Trianon
summary: Peace treaty that reduced Hungary to a third of its prewar territory, a lasting national grievance.

name: Horthy Regency
summary: Admiral Miklos Horthy ruled Hungary as regent of a kingdom without a king, allying with Nazi Germany.

name: Hungarian People's Republic
summary: Communist Hungary under Rakosi then Kadar's 'goulash communism' after the crushed 1956 revolution.

name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
summary: National uprising against Soviet domination, crushed by Red Army intervention with thousands killed.

name: Hungary
summary: Democratic republic since 1989, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004; governed by Viktor Orban since 2010.

name: Kingdom of Bohemia under the Habsburgs
summary: Bohemian crown lands within the Habsburg realm, Germanised after 1620 and industrialised in the 19th century.

name: Battle of White Mountain
summary: Catholic victory outside Prague that ended Bohemian independence and began forced re-Catholicisation.

name: Czechoslovakia
summary: State of Czechs and Slovaks founded in 1918, dismembered in 1938-39, communist from 1948, split in 1993.

name: Presidency of Tomas Masaryk
summary: Founding president who made interwar Czechoslovakia central Europe's most durable democracy.

name: Sudeten Crisis and Annexation
summary: German-speaking borderlands ceded under the Munich Agreement, followed by occupation in March 1939.

name: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
summary: German protectorate over the Czech lands, site of Heydrich's assassination and the Lidice massacre.

name: Czechoslovak Coup of 1948
summary: Communist seizure of power in February 1948 that ended postwar pluralism.

name: Prague Spring
summary: Dubcek's 'socialism with a human face', crushed by a Warsaw Pact invasion in August 1968.

name: Velvet Revolution
summary: Non-violent mass protests that ended communist rule and made Vaclav Havel president.

name: Velvet Divorce
summary: Peaceful split of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on 1 January 1993.

name: Czech Republic
summary: Central European republic since 1993, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004.

name: Slovakia
summary: Independent Slovak republic since 1993, in NATO and the EU from 2004 and the euro from 2009.

name: Slovak State
summary: German client state under Jozef Tiso, which deported most Slovak Jews and faced the 1944 national uprising.

name: Greek War of Independence
summary: Revolt against Ottoman rule, won with British, French and Russian help at Navarino and by Russian invasion.

name: First Hellenic Republic
summary: Provisional revolutionary government under Kapodistrias until the powers imposed a monarchy.

name: Kingdom of Greece
summary: Monarchy created by the great powers, which expanded through the Balkan Wars and collapsed after the Asia Minor defeat.

name: Reign of Otto of Greece
summary: Bavarian prince installed as first king of Greece, deposed by a military revolt.

name: Reign of George I of Greece
summary: Long-reigning Danish-born king who gained the Ionian Islands, Thessaly and Macedonia; assassinated in 1913.

name: Balkan Wars
summary: Two wars that expelled the Ottomans from most of Europe and then set the victors against each other over Macedonia.

name: Greco-Turkish War
summary: Greek invasion of Anatolia defeated by Kemal's forces, ending with the burning of Smyrna.

name: Greek-Turkish Population Exchange
summary: Compulsory exchange under the Lausanne Convention that uprooted about 1.6 million people.

name: Second Hellenic Republic
summary: Interwar republic of coups and refugee resettlement, ended by the restoration of the monarchy.

name: Metaxas Regime
summary: Authoritarian '4th of August' government that rejected Mussolini's 1940 ultimatum with 'Oxi'.

name: Axis Occupation of Greece
summary: German, Italian and Bulgarian occupation with famine, the destruction of Greek Jewry and mass resistance.

name: Greek Civil War
summary: Communist insurgency defeated by the government with British and then American support under the Truman Doctrine.

name: Greek Military Junta
summary: Colonels' dictatorship that abolished the monarchy and fell after the Cyprus crisis.

name: Hellenic Republic
summary: Democratic Greece since the fall of the junta, an EU member since 1981 and euro member since 2001.

name: Greek Government-Debt Crisis
summary: Sovereign-debt collapse and three bailout programmes with severe austerity inside the eurozone.

name: First Serbian Uprising
summary: Revolt under Karadjordje against Ottoman rule that began modern Serbian statehood.

name: Principality of Serbia
summary: Autonomous then independent Serbian principality under the Obrenovic and Karadjordjevic houses.

name: Kingdom of Serbia
summary: Independent kingdom that won the Balkan Wars, suffered occupation in 1915 and became the core of Yugoslavia.

name: Congress of Berlin
summary: Great-power settlement that recognised Serbia, Montenegro and Romania and shrank Bulgaria.

name: Principality of Bulgaria
summary: Autonomous Ottoman tributary created at Berlin, which absorbed Eastern Rumelia in 1885.

name: Kingdom of Bulgaria
summary: Independent tsardom that fought on the losing side in both world wars.

name: People's Republic of Bulgaria
summary: Communist state closely tied to the USSR under Todor Zhivkov for 35 years.

name: Republic of Bulgaria
summary: Democratic republic since 1990, in NATO from 2004 and the EU from 2007.

name: Wallachia and Moldavia
summary: Ottoman tributary principalities, later under Phanariot then Russian-protected regimes, united in 1859.

name: United Principalities of Romania
summary: Union under Alexandru Ioan Cuza and then Carol I, independent from the Ottomans in 1878.

name: Kingdom of Romania
summary: Kingdom that doubled in size as Greater Romania in 1918 and fell to communism after 1944.

name: Socialist Republic of Romania
summary: Communist Romania, independent-minded under Ceausescu's increasingly repressive personality cult.

name: Romanian Revolution of 1989
summary: Violent uprising that overthrew and executed Nicolae Ceausescu in December 1989.

name: Romania
summary: Democratic republic since 1989, in NATO from 2004 and the EU from 2007.

name: Principality and Kingdom of Montenegro
summary: Independent mountain state under the Petrovic-Njegos dynasty, recognised in 1878 and merged into Yugoslavia.

name: Albanian Declaration of Independence
summary: Ismail Qemali proclaimed Albanian independence at Vlore during the First Balkan War.

name: Kingdom of Albania
summary: Zog I's kingdom, increasingly an Italian dependency until Italy invaded in 1939.

name: People's Socialist Republic of Albania
summary: Enver Hoxha's isolated Stalinist state, which broke with Yugoslavia, the USSR and finally China.

name: Republic of Albania
summary: Post-communist democracy since 1992, a NATO member from 2009 and EU candidate.

name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
summary: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes renamed Yugoslavia in 1929, a royal dictatorship destroyed by Axis invasion.
aliases: Kingdom of Serbs Croats and Slovenes

name: Axis Invasion of Yugoslavia
summary: German-led attack that dismembered the kingdom and produced the Ustase state and partisan resistance.

name: Independent State of Croatia
summary: Ustase puppet state under Ante Pavelic responsible for the Jasenovac camps and genocide of Serbs, Jews and Roma.

name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
summary: Tito's federation of six republics, non-aligned and self-managing, which disintegrated in war after his death.

name: Rule of Josip Broz Tito
summary: Partisan leader turned president for life who split with Stalin in 1948 and led the Non-Aligned Movement.

name: Yugoslav Wars
summary: Series of wars accompanying Yugoslavia's breakup, with ethnic cleansing, siege warfare and NATO intervention.

name: Slovenian Ten-Day War
summary: Brief conflict after Slovenia's independence declaration, ending with Yugoslav withdrawal.

name: Croatian War of Independence
summary: War between Croatia and Serb forces, including the siege of Dubrovnik and Vukovar and Operation Storm.

name: Bosnian War
summary: Three-way war with the siege of Sarajevo and genocide at Srebrenica, ended by the Dayton Agreement.

name: Srebrenica Genocide
summary: Massacre of over 8,000 Bosniak men and boys by Bosnian Serb forces in a UN safe area.

name: Dayton Agreement
summary: US-brokered peace ending the Bosnian War and creating a federal state of two entities.

name: Kosovo War
summary: Insurgency and Serbian counter-offensive that triggered NATO's 78-day bombing campaign and UN administration.

name: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
summary: Rump federation of Serbia and Montenegro under Slobodan Milosevic, renamed Serbia and Montenegro in 2003.

name: Serbia and Montenegro
summary: Loose state union that dissolved when Montenegro voted for independence in 2006.

name: Republic of Serbia
summary: Independent Serbia since Montenegro's separation; an EU candidate that does not recognise Kosovo.

name: Montenegro
summary: Adriatic republic independent since a 2006 referendum, a NATO member since 2017.

name: Republic of Croatia
summary: Independent since 1991, a NATO member from 2009, EU from 2013 and eurozone from 2023.

name: Republic of Slovenia
summary: First Yugoslav republic to secede successfully; joined the EU and NATO in 2004 and the euro in 2007.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary: Independent state since 1992, governed since Dayton as a federation of two entities with international oversight.

name: North Macedonia
summary: Independent since 1991; renamed under the 2018 Prespa Agreement and a NATO member since 2020.

name: Republic of Kosovo
summary: Declared independence from Serbia in 2008, recognised by about half the world's states.

name: Ireland
summary: Independent Irish state, a republic from 1949, neutral, and an EU member since 1973.

name: Irish War of Independence
summary: Guerrilla war by the IRA that led to the Anglo-Irish Treaty and the Irish Free State.

name: Irish Civil War
summary: Conflict between pro- and anti-Treaty forces over partition and the oath to the crown.

name: Great Irish Famine
summary: Potato blight famine that killed about a million people and drove a million more to emigrate.

name: The Troubles
summary: Three decades of conflict between republicans, loyalists and the British state, ended by the Good Friday Agreement.

name: Good Friday Agreement
summary: Peace settlement creating power-sharing devolution and North-South institutions.

name: Republic of Malta
summary: Mediterranean island state independent from Britain in 1964, a republic from 1974 and EU member from 2004.

name: Hospitaller Malta
summary: Rule of the Knights of St John, who withstood the Great Siege of 1565 and built Valletta.

name: Tsardom of Russia
summary: Muscovite state proclaimed a tsardom under Ivan IV, which conquered Kazan and Siberia and survived the Time of Troubles.

name: Reign of Ivan IV the Terrible
summary: First crowned tsar; conquered Kazan and Astrakhan, launched the Livonian War and terrorised the boyars with the oprichnina.

name: Russian Conquest of Siberia
summary: Cossack and merchant expansion across northern Asia to the Pacific, driven by the fur trade.

name: Time of Troubles
summary: Dynastic vacuum, famine, false Dmitrys and Polish-Swedish intervention, ended by the election of the Romanovs.

name: House of Romanov
summary: Dynasty that ruled Russia for three centuries, from Michael I to Nicholas II.

name: Reign of Peter the Great
summary: Westernising tsar who built St Petersburg and a navy, beat Sweden at Poltava and proclaimed the Russian Empire.

name: Founding of St Petersburg
summary: Peter I founded his new capital on the Neva as a window on Europe.

name: Russian Empire
summary: Empire proclaimed by Peter I that expanded into the Baltic, Poland, the Caucasus, Central Asia and Alaska before 1917.

name: Reign of Catherine the Great
summary: Enlightened empress who annexed Crimea and much of Poland, expanded serfdom and corresponded with the philosophes.

name: Pugachev's Rebellion
summary: Massive Cossack and peasant revolt suppressed by Catherine II, hardening noble control over serfs.

name: Reign of Alexander I of Russia
summary: Tsar who defeated Napoleon's invasion, entered Paris and shaped the Holy Alliance at Vienna.

name: French Invasion of Russia
summary: Napoleon's Grande Armee reached Moscow and was destroyed in retreat, losing most of half a million men.

name: Decembrist Revolt
summary: Failed liberal officers' coup at Nicholas I's accession, followed by decades of repression.

name: Reign of Nicholas I
summary: Autocracy of orthodoxy and censorship, the 'gendarme of Europe', ending in defeat in the Crimean War.

name: Crimean War
summary: Russia's defeat by Britain, France, the Ottomans and Piedmont, which exposed its backwardness and forced reform.

name: Reign of Alexander II
summary: Tsar-liberator who emancipated the serfs and reformed law and local government; assassinated in 1881.

name: Emancipation of the Serfs
summary: Alexander II's manifesto freeing some 23 million serfs, with land redemption payments.

name: Reign of Alexander III
summary: Counter-reforming tsar of Russification, pogroms and rapid railway-led industrialisation.

name: Reign of Nicholas II
summary: Last tsar: defeat by Japan, the 1905 revolution, the Duma, war in 1914 and abdication in 1917.

name: Russo-Japanese War
summary: Japan's victory over Russia at Port Arthur, Mukden and Tsushima, the first modern Asian defeat of a European power.

name: Russian Revolution of 1905
summary: Bloody Sunday, mass strikes and mutinies forced Nicholas II to grant the October Manifesto and a Duma.

name: February Revolution
summary: Petrograd bread riots and mutiny toppled the tsar and created a Provisional Government and soviets.

name: Russian Provisional Government
summary: Liberal-socialist government under Lvov then Kerensky that kept Russia in the war and fell in October.

name: October Revolution
summary: Bolshevik seizure of power in Petrograd under Lenin and Trotsky, creating the world's first communist state.

name: Russian Civil War
summary: Reds defeated Whites, nationalists and Allied interventions at a cost of millions of lives and famine.

name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
summary: Bolshevik peace with Germany that surrendered Ukraine, the Baltics and Poland, annulled in November 1918.

name: War Communism
summary: Forced grain requisitioning and nationalisation during the civil war, ended by famine and the New Economic Policy.

name: Soviet Union
summary: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics: one-party communist federation, industrial and nuclear superpower, dissolved in December 1991.

name: Lenin's Leadership of Soviet Russia
summary: Founder of the Bolshevik state, architect of the one-party system, the Comintern and the NEP.

name: New Economic Policy
summary: Partial market restoration in agriculture and small trade that revived the economy after war communism.

name: Stalin's Rule of the Soviet Union
summary: Collectivisation, five-year plans, terror and victory over Germany under a totalitarian personality cult.

name: Soviet Collectivisation
summary: Forced collectivisation of agriculture and dekulakisation, causing famine across Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Russia.

name: Holodomor
summary: Man-made famine in Soviet Ukraine that killed roughly four million people, recognised by many states as genocide.

name: Great Purge
summary: Stalin's terror: show trials, mass executions of some 700,000 people and destruction of the party and army leadership.

name: Gulag System
summary: Vast network of forced-labour camps that held millions of prisoners, wound down after Stalin's death.

name: Great Patriotic War
summary: Soviet war against Germany from Barbarossa to Berlin, with roughly 27 million Soviet dead.

name: Khrushchev Era
summary: De-Stalinisation, the Secret Speech, Sputnik, the Virgin Lands and the Cuban missile crisis, ending in his ouster.

name: Khrushchev Thaw
summary: Relative cultural and political liberalisation after the denunciation of Stalin's crimes.

name: Brezhnev Era
summary: Stagnation and stability: Prague Spring suppression, detente, oil-funded consumerism and the Afghan invasion.

name: Andropov and Chernenko Interregnum
summary: Two brief, ailing general secretaries between Brezhnev and Gorbachev.

name: Gorbachev Era
summary: Perestroika, glasnost and arms control that ended the Cold War and unintentionally dissolved the USSR.

name: Chernobyl Disaster
summary: Reactor explosion on 26 April 1986 that spread radiation across Europe and discredited Soviet secrecy.

name: August Coup
summary: Failed hardline putsch against Gorbachev that accelerated the union's collapse and Yeltsin's rise.

name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
summary: Belovezha Accords and Gorbachev's resignation ended the USSR on 26 December 1991, creating fifteen states.

name: Russian Federation
summary: Successor state to the USSR: shock-therapy transition, Chechen wars, oil-fuelled recovery and wars in Georgia and Ukraine.

name: Presidency of Boris Yeltsin
summary: First Russian president: market shock therapy, the 1993 constitutional crisis, Chechnya and the 1998 default.

name: First Chechen War
summary: Russian invasion of separatist Chechnya ending in a humiliating ceasefire at Khasavyurt.

name: Second Chechen War
summary: Renewed campaign that reasserted Moscow's control over Chechnya under Kadyrov.

name: Rule of Vladimir Putin
summary: President from 2000 (prime minister 2008-12), centralising power, curbing media and pursuing war in Ukraine.

name: Presidency of Dmitry Medvedev
summary: Interim presidency with Putin as premier; the 2008 Georgia war and the financial crisis.

name: Russo-Georgian War
summary: Five-day war over South Ossetia and Abkhazia that Russia won and followed by recognising both.

name: Russian Annexation of Crimea
summary: Russian forces seized Crimea and staged a referendum, triggering Western sanctions and war in the Donbas.

name: War in Donbas
summary: Russian-backed separatist conflict in eastern Ukraine that killed over 13,000 before the full invasion.

name: Russian Invasion of Ukraine
summary: Full-scale Russian invasion from 24 February 2022, Europe's largest war since 1945.

name: Cossack Hetmanate
summary: Cossack state under Khmelnytsky that allied with Muscovy at Pereiaslav and was absorbed by Russia.

name: Ukrainian People's Republic
summary: Short-lived independent Ukraine under Hrushevsky, Skoropadsky and Petliura, defeated by Bolshevik forces.

name: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: Soviet Ukraine, site of the Holodomor, brutal Nazi occupation and postwar industrialisation.

name: Ukraine
summary: Independent since the 1991 referendum; the Orange Revolution, Euromaidan and war with Russia have shaped its statehood.

name: Orange Revolution
summary: Mass protests that overturned a rigged presidential election in favour of Viktor Yushchenko.

name: Euromaidan
summary: Kyiv protests against a shelved EU agreement that ousted President Yanukovych.

name: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: Soviet Belarus, which lost about a quarter of its population in the Second World War.

name: Republic of Belarus
summary: Independent since 1991 and ruled by Alexander Lukashenko since 1994 in close alignment with Russia.

name: Republic of Moldova
summary: Former Soviet republic independent since 1991, with the breakaway Transnistria region and EU candidate status.

name: Transnistria
summary: Unrecognised Russian-backed breakaway statelet on the left bank of the Dniester.

name: Crimean Khanate
summary: Tatar successor of the Golden Horde, an Ottoman vassal and slave-raiding power, annexed by Russia in 1783.

name: Khanate of Khiva
summary: Uzbek khanate on the Amu Darya that became a Russian protectorate in 1873 and a Soviet republic in 1920.

name: Emirate of Bukhara
summary: Manghit emirate, a Russian protectorate from 1868, overthrown by the Red Army in 1920.

name: Khanate of Kokand
summary: Ferghana valley khanate annexed outright by Russia in 1876.

name: Russian Conquest of Central Asia
summary: Tsarist campaigns that absorbed Turkestan and the steppe, part of the Great Game with Britain.

name: The Great Game
summary: Anglo-Russian strategic rivalry over Afghanistan, Persia and Turkestan, settled by the 1907 convention.

name: Basmachi Revolt
summary: Muslim resistance to Russian and Soviet rule across Turkestan, suppressed by the Red Army.

name: Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: Soviet Kazakhstan: famine under collectivisation, Virgin Lands campaign, Semipalatinsk nuclear tests and Baikonur.

name: Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Largest Central Asian state, independent in 1991, oil-rich and ruled by Nazarbayev until 2019.

name: Republic of Uzbekistan
summary: Most populous Central Asian state, independent in 1991, ruled by Karimov until 2016.

name: Turkmenistan
summary: Gas-rich neutral state independent in 1991 under Niyazov's personality cult and his successors.

name: Kyrgyz Republic
summary: Central Asian republic independent in 1991, with revolutions in 2005, 2010 and 2020.

name: Republic of Tajikistan
summary: Independent in 1991 and scarred by a civil war from 1992 to 1997; ruled by Emomali Rahmon.

name: Tajik Civil War
summary: Post-Soviet conflict between government and Islamist-democratic opposition that killed tens of thousands.

name: Desiccation of the Aral Sea
summary: Soviet irrigation of cotton lands shrank the Aral Sea by most of its volume, a landmark ecological disaster.

name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti
summary: Unified eastern Georgian kingdom that sought Russian protection and was annexed by Russia in 1801.

name: Democratic Republic of Georgia
summary: Independent Menshevik-led Georgia, invaded and sovietised by the Red Army in 1921.

name: Georgia
summary: Independent since 1991; the Rose Revolution, the 2008 war with Russia and EU aspirations have defined it.

name: Rose Revolution
summary: Peaceful protests that removed Eduard Shevardnadze and brought Mikheil Saakashvili to power.

name: First Republic of Armenia
summary: Independent Armenia after Ottoman collapse, overwhelmed by Turkish and Soviet forces.

name: Republic of Armenia
summary: Independent since 1991, shaped by the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict with Azerbaijan.

name: Republic of Azerbaijan
summary: Oil-rich Caspian republic independent in 1991, ruled by the Aliyev family since 1993.

name: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic
summary: First secular democratic republic in the Muslim world, sovietised in 1920.

name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
summary: War between Armenians and Azerbaijan over Karabakh that displaced about a million people.

name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
summary: Forty-four-day Azerbaijani victory that recovered most occupied territory; Karabakh fell entirely in 2023.

name: New France
summary: French colonial empire in North America from Acadia and Quebec to Louisiana, ceded to Britain and Spain in 1763.

name: Jacques Cartier's Voyages
summary: Three French voyages that claimed the St Lawrence for France and named Canada.

name: Founding of Quebec City
summary: Samuel de Champlain established the habitation at Quebec, the permanent base of New France.

name: Hudson's Bay Company
summary: Royal-chartered fur-trade company that governed Rupert's Land until selling it to Canada in 1870.

name: Beaver Wars
summary: Long Iroquois-French-Algonquian conflicts over the fur trade, ended by the Great Peace of Montreal.

name: Expulsion of the Acadians
summary: British deportation of some 10,000 French-speaking Acadians from the Maritimes.

name: Conquest of Canada
summary: French and Indian War campaigns culminating at the Plains of Abraham in 1759 and the Treaty of Paris.
aliases: Battle of the Plains of Abraham

name: Province of Quebec (British)
summary: British colony where the Quebec Act of 1774 guaranteed French civil law and Catholic rights.

name: Upper and Lower Canada
summary: Two colonies created by the Constitutional Act, each with an elected assembly, joined after the 1837 rebellions.

name: War of 1812 in Canada
summary: American invasions repelled by British regulars, Canadian militia and Indigenous allies under Tecumseh and Brock.

name: Rebellions of 1837-38
summary: Patriote and Upper Canadian revolts for responsible government, suppressed but leading to the Durham Report.

name: Province of Canada
summary: United colony of Canada East and West that won responsible government in 1848.

name: Canadian Confederation
summary: British North America Act of 1 July 1867 united Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as a federal dominion.

name: Canada
summary: Federal dominion of 1867 that grew to ten provinces and three territories and became fully sovereign by stages.

name: Red River Resistance
summary: Louis Riel's Metis provisional government, which led to Manitoba's creation as a province.

name: Manitoba Joins Canada
summary: Manitoba entered Confederation as the fifth province after the Red River Resistance.

name: British Columbia Joins Canada
summary: BC entered Confederation on the promise of a transcontinental railway.

name: Prince Edward Island Joins Canada
summary: PEI entered Confederation in 1873, burdened by railway debt.

name: Completion of the Canadian Pacific Railway
summary: Last spike at Craigellachie linked Canada by rail, built largely by Chinese labourers.

name: North-West Rebellion
summary: Metis and Cree resistance led by Riel and Big Bear, defeated and followed by Riel's execution.

name: Creation of Alberta and Saskatchewan
summary: Two new prairie provinces carved from the North-West Territories.

name: Canada in the First World War
summary: More than 600,000 served; Vimy Ridge and the conscription crisis shaped national identity.

name: Statute of Westminster
summary: British act recognising the legislative independence of the dominions.

name: Newfoundland Joins Canada
summary: Newfoundland became Canada's tenth province after two close referendums.

name: Quiet Revolution
summary: Rapid secularisation and state-building in Quebec that transformed its politics and fuelled sovereigntism.

name: October Crisis
summary: FLQ kidnappings and the murder of Pierre Laporte led Trudeau to invoke the War Measures Act.

name: Quebec Referendum of 1980
summary: Sovereignty-association rejected by 60 percent of Quebec voters.

name: Constitution Act, 1982
summary: Patriation of the constitution with the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, without Quebec's consent.

name: Quebec Referendum of 1995
summary: Sovereignty narrowly defeated by 50.6 to 49.4 percent.

name: Creation of Nunavut
summary: New Inuit-majority territory established from the eastern Northwest Territories.

name: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada
summary: Inquiry into residential schools that documented cultural genocide against Indigenous peoples.

name: Canadian Indian Residential School System
summary: Church-run, state-funded schools that forcibly assimilated Indigenous children, with thousands of deaths.

name: Premiership of John A. Macdonald
summary: First prime minister (1867-73, 1878-91): Confederation, the CPR, the National Policy and the Riel executions.

name: Premiership of Alexander Mackenzie
summary: Liberal prime minister who created the Supreme Court and the secret ballot.

name: Premiership of John Abbott
summary: Conservative caretaker prime minister after Macdonald's death.

name: Premiership of John Thompson
summary: Prime minister who codified the Criminal Code and died in office at Windsor Castle.

name: Premiership of Mackenzie Bowell
summary: Prime minister brought down by cabinet revolt over the Manitoba schools question.

name: Premiership of Charles Tupper
summary: Shortest-serving Canadian prime minister, in office 69 days.

name: Premiership of Wilfrid Laurier
summary: First francophone prime minister: immigration boom, two new provinces and compromise on imperial questions.

name: Premiership of Robert Borden
summary: Wartime prime minister: conscription crisis, Union government and a separate Canadian seat at Versailles.

name: Premiership of Arthur Meighen
summary: Conservative prime minister in 1920-21 and briefly in 1926 during the King-Byng affair.

name: Premiership of William Lyon Mackenzie King
summary: Longest-serving prime minister in the Commonwealth: Depression, wartime leadership and the welfare state's start.

name: Premiership of R. B. Bennett
summary: Depression-era Conservative prime minister who created the Bank of Canada and the CBC's predecessor.

name: Premiership of Louis St-Laurent
summary: 'Uncle Louis' oversaw NATO membership, Newfoundland's entry and the St Lawrence Seaway.

name: Premiership of John Diefenbaker
summary: Prairie Conservative: the Bill of Rights, Indigenous voting rights and the Avro Arrow cancellation.

name: Premiership of Lester Pearson
summary: Nobel peace laureate whose minority governments created medicare, the maple leaf flag and the Canada Pension Plan.

name: Premiership of Pierre Trudeau
summary: Prime minister 1968-79 and 1980-84: bilingualism, multiculturalism, the October Crisis and patriation with the Charter.

name: Premiership of Joe Clark
summary: Nine-month Progressive Conservative minority government defeated on its budget.

name: Premiership of John Turner
summary: Liberal prime minister for 79 days before a landslide defeat.

name: Premiership of Brian Mulroney
summary: Free trade with the United States, the GST, failed Meech Lake and Charlottetown accords, and anti-apartheid diplomacy.

name: Premiership of Kim Campbell
summary: Canada's first woman prime minister, in office for about four months.

name: Premiership of Jean Chretien
summary: Deficit elimination, the 1995 referendum and the Clarity Act, and refusal to join the Iraq war.

name: Premiership of Paul Martin
summary: Prime minister who legalised same-sex marriage nationally and faced the sponsorship scandal.

name: Premiership of Stephen Harper
summary: Conservative prime minister through the 2008 crisis, the residential schools apology and Afghan combat operations.

name: Premiership of Justin Trudeau
summary: Liberal prime minister: cannabis legalisation, carbon pricing, USMCA and the COVID-19 response.

name: Premiership of Mark Carney
summary: Former central banker who became Liberal leader and prime minister in 2025.

name: Viceroyalty of New Spain
summary: Spanish viceroyalty ruling Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and the Philippines from Mexico City.

name: Spanish Conquest of the Aztec Empire
summary: Cortes and Indigenous allies destroyed Tenochtitlan, beginning Spanish rule in Mesoamerica.

name: Mexican War of Independence
summary: Eleven-year struggle begun by Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores and completed by Iturbide's Plan of Iguala.

name: First Mexican Empire
summary: Agustin de Iturbide's brief empire, which included Central America.

name: First Mexican Republic
summary: Federal republic under the 1824 constitution, riven by centralist-federalist conflict.

name: Era of Santa Anna
summary: Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna held the presidency eleven times amid the loss of Texas and the war with the United States.

name: Texas Revolution
summary: Anglo-Texan and Tejano revolt that won independence after the Alamo and San Jacinto.

name: Mexican-American War
summary: War that cost Mexico half its territory under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.

name: La Reforma
summary: Liberal reforms under Juarez that curbed church and army privilege and produced the 1857 constitution.

name: War of the Reform
summary: Civil war between liberals and conservatives won by Juarez's liberals.

name: Second Mexican Empire
summary: French-imposed empire of Maximilian of Habsburg, which collapsed when France withdrew; he was executed at Queretaro.

name: Presidency of Benito Juarez
summary: Zapotec liberal who led resistance to the French intervention and restored the republic.

name: Porfiriato
summary: Porfirio Diaz's 35-year rule: railways, foreign investment and repression, ended by the Revolution.

name: Mexican Revolution
summary: Decade of civil war involving Madero, Villa, Zapata, Carranza and Obregon, costing perhaps a million lives.

name: Mexican Constitution of 1917
summary: Landmark constitution establishing land reform, labour rights and state ownership of subsoil resources.

name: Cristero War
summary: Catholic rural rebellion against anticlerical enforcement, settled by negotiated modus vivendi.

name: Rule of the Institutional Revolutionary Party
summary: Single dominant party governed Mexico for 71 years under a rotating presidential system.

name: Presidency of Lazaro Cardenas
summary: Land redistribution, support for Spanish republicans and the 1938 nationalisation of oil as Pemex.

name: Mexican Oil Expropriation
summary: Cardenas nationalised foreign oil companies and created Pemex, a founding act of economic sovereignty.

name: Tlatelolco Massacre
summary: Army killing of student protesters in Mexico City days before the Olympics.

name: Mexican Peso Crisis
summary: Currency collapse and US-led bailout known as the Tequila Crisis.

name: Zapatista Uprising
summary: EZLN indigenous rebellion in Chiapas launched as NAFTA took effect.

name: Mexican Democratic Transition
summary: Vicente Fox's victory ended 71 years of PRI presidential rule.

name: Mexican Drug War
summary: Militarised campaign against cartels launched by Felipe Calderon, with well over 300,000 dead.

name: United Mexican States
summary: Federal republic of 31 states and a capital, Latin America's second-largest economy.

name: Presidency of Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador
summary: Leftist president who built Morena's dominance and expanded social programmes and military infrastructure roles.

name: Presidency of Claudia Sheinbaum
summary: Mexico's first woman president, elected in 2024 as AMLO's successor.

name: Colonial Brazil
summary: Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold and enslaved African labour, with its capital at Salvador then Rio.

name: Portuguese Landing in Brazil
summary: Pedro Alvares Cabral reached the Brazilian coast in April 1500, claiming it for Portugal.

name: Dutch Brazil
summary: Dutch West India Company colony in Pernambuco under Johan Maurits, expelled by Luso-Brazilian forces.

name: Quilombo dos Palmares
summary: Large maroon polity of escaped enslaved people in Alagoas, destroyed after decades of resistance under Zumbi.

name: Minas Gerais Gold Rush
summary: Gold and diamond boom that shifted Brazil's centre south and funded Portuguese and British commerce.

name: Transfer of the Portuguese Court to Brazil
summary: The royal family fled Napoleon to Rio, opening Brazilian ports and elevating the colony.

name: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves
summary: Transatlantic kingdom in which Brazil was legally equal to Portugal.

name: Brazilian Independence
summary: Pedro I's Grito do Ipiranga on 7 September 1822 declared independence, achieved with little bloodshed.

name: Empire of Brazil
summary: Constitutional monarchy of the Americas under Pedro I and Pedro II, which abolished slavery and fell to a coup.

name: Reign of Pedro I of Brazil
summary: Founder of the empire who granted the 1824 constitution and abdicated to claim the Portuguese throne.

name: Reign of Pedro II of Brazil
summary: Long, stable reign of a scholar-emperor: the Paraguayan War, coffee expansion, abolition and deposition.

name: Paraguayan War
summary: Triple Alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay devastated Paraguay, killing a large share of its population.

name: Golden Law
summary: Abolition of slavery in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to end it.

name: First Brazilian Republic
summary: Oligarchic 'coffee with milk' republic of Sao Paulo and Minas elites, ended by Vargas's revolution.

name: Vargas Era
summary: Getulio Vargas ruled by revolution then dictatorship, creating labour laws, industry and the Estado Novo.

name: Estado Novo (Brazil)
summary: Vargas's corporatist dictatorship, which nonetheless joined the Allies in 1942.

name: Brazilian Second Republic
summary: Democratic period of developmentalism, the building of Brasilia and mounting political crisis.

name: Founding of Brasilia
summary: Kubitschek's modernist capital inaugurated in the interior, designed by Costa and Niemeyer.

name: Brazilian Military Dictatorship
