summary: Twenty-one years of army rule with censorship, torture and the 'economic miracle', ending in a gradual opening.

name: Federative Republic of Brazil
summary: Democratic Brazil under the 1988 constitution, with the Real Plan, commodity boom and impeachment crises.

name: Plano Real
summary: Currency stabilisation plan that ended hyperinflation and introduced the real.

name: Presidencies of Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
summary: Trade-unionist president 2003-2010 and again from 2023: Bolsa Familia, poverty reduction and diplomatic prominence.

name: Impeachment of Dilma Rousseff
summary: Brazil's first woman president removed amid recession and the Lava Jato corruption investigation.

name: Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro
summary: Right-wing populist presidency marked by Amazon deforestation, COVID-19 denial and the 2023 Brasilia riot.

name: Viceroyalty of Peru
summary: Spanish viceroyalty centred on Lima that governed most of South America and the Potosi silver economy.

name: Viceroyalty of New Granada
summary: Spanish viceroyalty covering Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, based at Bogota.

name: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
summary: Late Spanish viceroyalty based in Buenos Aires covering Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia.

name: Potosi Silver Complex
summary: Cerro Rico mines worked under the mita labour draft supplied much of the world's silver and financed Spain.

name: Bourbon Reforms
summary: Administrative, fiscal and military reforms that increased extraction and provoked creole resentment and revolt.

name: Rebellion of Tupac Amaru II
summary: Largest Andean uprising against Spanish rule, brutally suppressed after threatening Cusco.

name: Spanish American Wars of Independence
summary: Continental struggle that ended Spanish rule in the mainland Americas and created some fifteen republics.

name: Campaigns of Simon Bolivar
summary: The Liberator's campaigns from Venezuela over the Andes to Boyaca, Carabobo, Junin and Ayacucho.

name: Campaigns of Jose de San Martin
summary: Crossing of the Andes, liberation of Chile at Chacabuco and Maipu, and the proclamation of Peru's independence.

name: Battle of Ayacucho
summary: Sucre's victory that destroyed the last royalist army and sealed South American independence.

name: Gran Colombia
summary: Bolivar's union of Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, dissolved by regional rivalries.

name: Congress of Panama
summary: Bolivar's attempt at a league of American republics, an ancestor of Pan-Americanism.

name: Federal Republic of Central America
summary: Union of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica that fragmented into five states.

name: United Provinces of the Rio de la Plata
summary: Post-revolutionary confederation that declared independence at Tucuman in 1816 amid unitarian-federalist civil war.

name: May Revolution
summary: Buenos Aires cabildo abierto deposed the viceroy, beginning Argentine self-government.

name: Argentine Declaration of Independence
summary: Congress of Tucuman declared independence from Spain on 9 July 1816.

name: Rule of Juan Manuel de Rosas
summary: Federalist caudillo who dominated the Argentine Confederation until defeat at Caseros.

name: Argentine Republic
summary: Federal republic constituted in 1853, transformed by mass European immigration and the grain and beef export boom.

name: Conquest of the Desert
summary: Military campaigns that seized Indigenous Patagonian lands and opened them to settlement.

name: Peronism
summary: Mass movement founded by Juan and Eva Peron combining labour rights, nationalism and personalist leadership.

name: Argentine Dirty War
summary: Military junta's campaign of disappearances that killed up to 30,000 people.

name: Falklands War
summary: Argentine invasion of the Falklands defeated by Britain, precipitating the junta's collapse.

name: Argentine Economic Crisis of 2001
summary: Default, corralito bank freeze and five presidents in two weeks.

name: Captaincy General of Chile
summary: Spanish colony hemmed in by Mapuche resistance beyond the Bio-Bio river.

name: Chilean War of Independence
summary: Patria Vieja, reconquest and final liberation by San Martin and O'Higgins at Chacabuco and Maipu.

name: Republic of Chile
summary: South American republic stabilised by Portales's 1833 constitution, later shaped by nitrates, copper and the Pinochet era.

name: War of the Pacific
summary: Chile defeated Peru and Bolivia, taking nitrate provinces and leaving Bolivia landlocked.

name: Occupation of Araucania
summary: Chilean military conquest of Mapuche territory south of the Bio-Bio.

name: Presidency of Salvador Allende
summary: First elected Marxist president, who nationalised copper and was overthrown in the 11 September 1973 coup.

name: Pinochet Dictatorship
summary: Military regime with over 3,000 killed and tens of thousands tortured, alongside radical free-market reform.

name: Republic of Peru
summary: Andean republic independent from 1821, shaped by guano and nitrate booms, military rule and the Shining Path conflict.

name: Shining Path Insurgency
summary: Maoist insurgency and state counterinsurgency that killed about 70,000 people.

name: Fujimori Government
summary: Alberto Fujimori defeated hyperinflation and Sendero but ruled by self-coup and corruption.

name: Republic of Colombia
summary: Andean-Caribbean republic, successor to New Granada, marked by two-party civil wars and a long internal conflict.

name: Thousand Days' War
summary: Liberal-Conservative civil war that killed some 100,000 and preceded Panama's secession.

name: La Violencia
summary: Partisan civil conflict triggered by Gaitan's assassination and the Bogotazo, killing about 200,000.

name: Colombian Armed Conflict
summary: Long war among FARC, ELN, paramilitaries, cartels and the state, partly ended by the 2016 peace accord.

name: Colombian Peace Agreement
summary: Havana accord that demobilised the FARC and won Santos the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Republic of Venezuela
summary: Caribbean-Andean republic that left Gran Colombia in 1830, later transformed by oil and by Chavismo.

name: Venezuelan Declaration of Independence
summary: First Venezuelan republic declared independence on 5 July 1811; it soon fell, beginning years of war.

name: Dictatorship of Juan Vicente Gomez
summary: Long personal rule during which oil made Venezuela a major exporter.

name: Punto Fijo Democracy
summary: Forty years of two-party democracy funded by oil, collapsing after the 1989 Caracazo riots.

name: Presidency of Hugo Chavez
summary: Bolivarian Revolution: new constitution, oil-funded social missions and confrontation with the United States.

name: Presidency of Nicolas Maduro
summary: Rule marked by economic collapse, hyperinflation, disputed elections and the emigration of millions.

name: Plurinational State of Bolivia
summary: Andean republic named for Bolivar, which lost its coast and Chaco lands and elected its first Indigenous president in 2005.

name: Chaco War
summary: Bolivia-Paraguay war over the Gran Chaco, won largely by Paraguay at great cost to both.

name: Bolivian National Revolution
summary: MNR revolution that nationalised tin, enfranchised Indigenous people and redistributed land.

name: Presidency of Evo Morales
summary: First Indigenous president: gas nationalisation, a plurinational constitution, and resignation amid disputed re-election.

name: Republic of Ecuador
summary: Andean-Pacific republic that left Gran Colombia in 1830; oil-exporting and dollarised since 2000.

name: Republic of Paraguay
summary: Landlocked republic independent from 1811, devastated in the Triple Alliance war and ruled by Stroessner for 35 years.

name: Stroessner Dictatorship
summary: Alfredo Stroessner's anticommunist regime, the longest in 20th-century South America.

name: Oriental Republic of Uruguay
summary: Buffer republic created by British mediation between Brazil and Argentina, later a pioneering welfare democracy.

name: Uruguayan Military Dictatorship
summary: Civil-military regime that imprisoned and tortured on a mass scale after the Tupamaro insurgency.

name: Republic of Guyana
summary: Former British Guiana, independent in 1966 and transformed by offshore oil since 2019.

name: Republic of Suriname
summary: Former Dutch Guiana, independent in 1975, with large emigration to the Netherlands.

name: French Guiana
summary: French territory and now overseas department, once a penal colony and now home to the Kourou spaceport.

name: Saint-Domingue
summary: France's richest colony, producing sugar and coffee with enslaved labour on a vast scale, destroyed by revolution.

name: Haitian Revolution
summary: Only successful large-scale slave revolt, which defeated French, Spanish and British forces and created Haiti.

name: Leadership of Toussaint Louverture
summary: Former slave who became governor of Saint-Domingue, abolished slavery and died in French captivity.

name: Haitian Declaration of Independence
summary: Dessalines proclaimed independence on 1 January 1804, the first Black republic and second American republic.

name: Republic of Haiti
summary: Independent since 1804, burdened by the French indemnity, US occupation, dictatorship and repeated state collapse.

name: United States Occupation of Haiti
summary: Nineteen-year American military rule that rewrote Haitian law and finances.

name: Duvalier Regime
summary: Francois 'Papa Doc' and Jean-Claude 'Baby Doc' Duvalier ruled with the Tontons Macoutes for 29 years.

name: 2010 Haiti Earthquake
summary: Magnitude 7.0 quake near Port-au-Prince that killed well over 100,000 people.

name: Dominican Republic
summary: Independent from Haiti in 1844, later occupied by the United States and ruled by Trujillo for three decades.

name: Trujillo Dictatorship
summary: Rafael Trujillo's cult-of-personality regime, responsible for the 1937 Parsley Massacre of Haitians.

name: Spanish Cuba
summary: Spain's sugar and tobacco colony and last major American possession, lost in 1898.

name: Ten Years' War
summary: First Cuban war of independence, ending in the Pact of Zanjon without independence.

name: Cuban War of Independence
summary: Marti- and Maceo-led revolt that drew in the United States and ended Spanish rule.

name: Republic of Cuba
summary: Cuban republic from 1902, under the Platt Amendment, then Batista, then communist rule since 1959.

name: Batista Regime
summary: Fulgencio Batista's corrupt dictatorship, overthrown by the 26th of July Movement.

name: Cuban Revolution
summary: Castro and Guevara's guerrilla campaign that took Havana on 1 January 1959.

name: Rule of Fidel Castro
summary: Nearly half a century leading communist Cuba through nationalisation, Soviet alliance and US embargo.

name: Bay of Pigs Invasion
summary: Failed CIA-backed exile landing at Playa Giron.

name: Cuban Missile Crisis
summary: Thirteen-day superpower confrontation over Soviet missiles in Cuba, the closest approach to nuclear war.

name: Special Period
summary: Severe economic crisis after Soviet subsidies ended, forcing rationing and limited market openings.

name: Presidency of Raul Castro
summary: Cautious economic liberalisation and the 2015 restoration of relations with the United States.

name: Commonwealth of Puerto Rico
summary: Spanish colony ceded to the United States in 1898, an unincorporated territory with commonwealth status since 1952.

name: Jamaica
summary: Former Spanish then British sugar colony, independent within the Commonwealth since 1962.

name: British Jamaica
summary: English conquest of 1655 created a plantation colony with maroon wars and the 1865 Morant Bay rebellion.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
summary: Oil- and gas-rich Caribbean state independent in 1962 and a republic since 1976.

name: Republic of Panama
summary: Seceded from Colombia with US backing in 1903; the canal returned to Panamanian control in 1999.

name: Panama Canal
summary: American-built interoceanic canal opened in 1914 after the failure of the French attempt.

name: United States Invasion of Panama
summary: Operation Just Cause removed Manuel Noriega from power.

name: Republic of Costa Rica
summary: Central American republic that abolished its army in 1949 and became the region's most stable democracy.

name: Republic of Nicaragua
summary: Central American republic shaped by US intervention, the Somoza dynasty and Sandinista rule.

name: Somoza Dynasty
summary: Family dictatorship backed by the National Guard and the United States, overthrown by the Sandinistas.

name: Sandinista Revolution
summary: FSLN insurrection that toppled Somoza and led to a decade of revolution and Contra war.

name: Contra War
summary: US-backed counter-revolutionary insurgency against the Sandinista government, tied to the Iran-Contra affair.

name: Republic of El Salvador
summary: Central American republic marked by the 1932 Matanza, a brutal civil war and postwar gang violence.

name: Salvadoran Civil War
summary: Twelve-year war between the US-backed government and the FMLN that killed some 75,000 people.

name: Republic of Guatemala
summary: Central American republic of the 1944 October Revolution, the 1954 coup and a genocidal civil war.

name: Guatemalan Coup of 1954
summary: CIA-organised overthrow of Jacobo Arbenz after his land reform threatened United Fruit.

name: Guatemalan Civil War
summary: Thirty-six-year conflict with about 200,000 dead, including genocide against Maya communities.

name: Republic of Honduras
summary: Central American republic long dominated by banana companies and by military politics.

name: Belize
summary: Former British Honduras, independent in 1981, the only English-speaking state in Central America.

name: Commonwealth of The Bahamas
summary: Archipelagic state independent from Britain in 1973.

name: Barbados
summary: Independent since 1966 and a republic since 2021, once a model English sugar colony.

name: Caribbean Community
summary: Regional integration organisation founded by the Treaty of Chaguaramas.

name: Abolition of Slavery in the Caribbean
summary: Successive emancipations from Haiti and the British colonies to Cuba, ending Atlantic plantation slavery.

name: Atlantic Slave Trade
summary: Forced transport of roughly 12.5 million Africans to the Americas, the foundation of the plantation economies.

name: Columbian Exchange
summary: Transfer of crops, animals, people and diseases between hemispheres that reshaped world population and diets.

name: Indigenous Demographic Collapse in the Americas
summary: Epidemics, war and forced labour killed a large majority of the pre-contact Indigenous population.

name: Late Sengoku Period
summary: Century of warring daimyo, firearms and castle towns, unified in stages by Nobunaga, Hideyoshi and Ieyasu.

name: Rule of Oda Nobunaga
summary: Warlord who seized Kyoto, broke the Buddhist militant orders and began unifying Japan before being betrayed at Honno-ji.

name: Rule of Toyotomi Hideyoshi
summary: Completed unification, froze the social order by sword hunts and land surveys, and invaded Korea twice.

name: Battle of Sekigahara
summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu's decisive victory that opened the way to the shogunate.

name: Tokugawa Shogunate
summary: Edo-based military government that gave Japan 265 years of peace under strict social order and limited foreign contact.

name: Sakoku
summary: Policy of closed borders permitting only limited Dutch, Chinese, Korean and Ryukyuan contact.

name: Shimabara Rebellion
summary: Christian and peasant revolt in Kyushu whose suppression sealed the proscription of Christianity.

name: Perry Expedition
summary: American gunboat diplomacy that forced Japan open with the Convention of Kanagawa.

name: Boshin War
summary: Civil war in which imperial loyalists defeated the shogunate and restored direct rule to the emperor.

name: Meiji Restoration
summary: Restoration of imperial rule and the start of rapid, state-led modernisation on Western models.

name: Empire of Japan
summary: Constitutional empire that industrialised, defeated China and Russia, built a colonial empire and lost the Pacific War.

name: Meiji Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Meiji: abolition of the samurai class, conscription, industry, constitution and imperial expansion.

name: Abolition of the Han
summary: Domains replaced by prefectures, ending feudal decentralisation.

name: Satsuma Rebellion
summary: Last samurai revolt, led by Saigo Takamori and crushed by the conscript army.

name: Meiji Constitution
summary: Prussian-inspired constitution granting a Diet while vesting sovereignty in the emperor.

name: First Sino-Japanese War
summary: Japanese victory that took Taiwan and ended Chinese suzerainty over Korea.

name: Japanese Annexation of Korea
summary: Treaty imposed after the 1905 protectorate made Korea a Japanese colony until 1945.

name: Taisho Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Taisho: party cabinets, universal male suffrage, rice riots and the 1923 Kanto earthquake.

name: Taisho Democracy
summary: Era of party government, mass politics and liberal culture, ended by militarist assassinations.

name: Great Kanto Earthquake
summary: Quake and firestorm that destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama and killed over 100,000.

name: Showa Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Hirohito: militarism, war, defeat, occupation and the postwar economic miracle.

name: Manchurian Incident
summary: Staged railway explosion used to justify the Japanese conquest of Manchuria.

name: Manchukuo
summary: Japanese puppet state in Manchuria nominally headed by the last Qing emperor Puyi.

name: February 26 Incident
summary: Failed young-officers' coup in Tokyo after which the army dominated the government.

name: Second Sino-Japanese War
summary: Full-scale Japanese invasion of China, part of the Second World War, with 15-20 million Chinese deaths.

name: Nanjing Massacre
summary: Mass killing and rape of Chinese civilians and prisoners after the fall of Nanjing.

name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
summary: Japanese carrier strike on 7 December 1941 that brought the United States into the Second World War.

name: Pacific War
summary: War between Japan and the Allies from Pearl Harbor to the surrender aboard USS Missouri.

name: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
summary: First use of nuclear weapons in war, killing well over 100,000 and hastening Japan's surrender.

name: Allied Occupation of Japan
summary: MacArthur's SCAP administration demilitarised Japan, wrote a new constitution and reformed land and industry.

name: Constitution of Japan
summary: Postwar constitution establishing popular sovereignty, a symbolic emperor and Article 9's renunciation of war.

name: Japan
summary: Postwar parliamentary state under the 1947 constitution, long the world's second-largest economy.

name: Treaty of San Francisco
summary: Peace treaty restoring Japanese sovereignty, accompanied by the US-Japan security treaty.

name: Japanese Economic Miracle
summary: Two decades of double-digit growth that made Japan an industrial giant, symbolised by the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

name: Japanese Asset Price Bubble and Lost Decades
summary: Stock and land bubble whose collapse produced prolonged stagnation and deflation.

name: Heisei Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Akihito: bubble collapse, Kobe earthquake, Aum attack and the 2011 triple disaster.

name: Great Hanshin Earthquake
summary: Kobe earthquake that killed over 6,000 and exposed weaknesses in disaster response.

name: Tohoku Earthquake and Fukushima Disaster
summary: Magnitude 9 quake, tsunami killing about 18,000, and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear meltdowns.

name: Reiwa Era
summary: Reign of Emperor Naruhito, beginning with his father's abdication in 2019.

name: Premierships of Shinzo Abe
summary: Japan's longest-serving prime minister (2006-07, 2012-20): Abenomics, security reinterpretation, assassinated in 2022.

name: Kingdom of Ryukyu (late)
summary: Okinawan maritime kingdom, a Satsuma vassal from 1609, annexed as Okinawa Prefecture in 1879.

name: Battle of Okinawa
summary: Eighty-two-day battle that killed perhaps a quarter of Okinawan civilians; US administration lasted to 1972.

name: Reversion of Okinawa
summary: Return of Okinawa to Japanese sovereignty, with US bases remaining.

name: Late Ming Dynasty
summary: Silver-fuelled commerce, population growth and crisis ending in rebellion, famine and Manchu conquest.

name: Qing Dynasty
summary: Last imperial dynasty, Manchu-ruled, which tripled China's territory then fell to internal revolt and foreign pressure.

name: Manchu Conquest of China
summary: Qing conquest from Beijing's fall in 1644 to the taking of Taiwan in 1683.

name: Kangxi Reign
summary: Sixty-one-year reign that consolidated Qing rule, took Taiwan and pushed into Mongolia and Tibet.

name: Qianlong Reign
summary: High Qing prosperity, conquest of Xinjiang and the Macartney embassy's rebuff.

name: Canton System
summary: Restriction of Western trade to Guangzhou through licensed hong merchants, ended by the Opium War.

name: First Opium War
summary: British victory forcing the Treaty of Nanking, ceding Hong Kong and opening treaty ports.

name: Unequal Treaties
summary: Century of imposed treaties granting extraterritoriality, indemnities and concessions to foreign powers.

name: Taiping Rebellion
summary: Millenarian civil war under Hong Xiuquan that killed perhaps 20-30 million people.

name: Second Opium War
summary: Anglo-French campaign that burned the Summer Palace and opened more of China to foreign trade and missions.

name: Self-Strengthening Movement
summary: Reform effort to adopt Western arms and industry while preserving Confucian institutions.

name: Regency of Empress Dowager Cixi
summary: Cixi dominated the Qing court for almost fifty years, blocking then belatedly embracing reform.

name: Hundred Days' Reform
summary: Guangxu Emperor's rapid reform programme, ended by Cixi's coup.

name: Boxer Rebellion
summary: Anti-foreign uprising crushed by an eight-nation force, followed by a crippling indemnity.

name: Xinhai Revolution
summary: Wuchang uprising and provincial secessions that ended two millennia of imperial rule.

name: Republic of China (mainland era)
summary: Republic founded by Sun Yat-sen, ruled by Yuan Shikai, warlords and then the Kuomintang until defeat by the communists.

name: Rule of Yuan Shikai
summary: First president who dissolved parliament and briefly proclaimed himself emperor in 1916.

name: Warlord Era
summary: Fragmentation of China among regional militarists after Yuan Shikai's death.

name: May Fourth Movement
summary: Student protests against the Versailles settlement that catalysed Chinese nationalism and the New Culture Movement.

name: Founding of the Chinese Communist Party
summary: First congress in Shanghai established the CCP with Comintern support.

name: Northern Expedition
summary: Chiang Kai-shek's campaign that nominally unified China under the Kuomintang.

name: Nanjing Decade
summary: Decade of Nationalist state-building interrupted by communist insurgency and Japanese encroachment.

name: Chinese Civil War
summary: Intermittent war between Nationalists and Communists, won by the CCP in 1949.

name: Long March
summary: Communist retreat of some 9,000 kilometres during which Mao secured party leadership.

name: People's Republic of China
summary: Communist state proclaimed by Mao on 1 October 1949, now the world's most populous nation for most of its history and second-largest economy.

name: Mao Era
summary: Land reform, Korean War, Great Leap Forward famine and Cultural Revolution under Mao Zedong.

name: Chinese Annexation of Tibet
summary: PLA entry into Tibet and the Seventeen Point Agreement, followed by the Dalai Lama's flight in 1959.

name: Great Leap Forward
summary: Forced collectivisation and industrial campaign that caused a famine killing tens of millions.

name: Sino-Soviet Split
summary: Ideological and strategic rupture between the communist giants, including border clashes in 1969.

name: Cultural Revolution
summary: Mao's mass campaign against 'revisionists' that closed schools, destroyed heritage and killed over a million.

name: Nixon's Visit to China
summary: Opening of relations that realigned Cold War diplomacy; the PRC took China's UN seat in 1971.

name: Deng Xiaoping Era
summary: Reform and opening: household farming, special economic zones, and the Tiananmen crackdown.

name: Reform and Opening Up
summary: Market reforms that lifted hundreds of millions from poverty and made China a manufacturing superpower.

name: One-Child Policy
summary: Coercive birth-limitation programme that reshaped China's demography.

name: Tiananmen Square Protests and Massacre
summary: Seven weeks of pro-democracy protests ended by military force on 3-4 June 1989.

name: Jiang Zemin Era
summary: Consolidation after Tiananmen, WTO accession and the Hong Kong and Macau handovers.

name: Hu Jintao Era
summary: Rapid growth, the 2008 Beijing Olympics and stimulus after the global financial crisis.

name: Xi Jinping Era
summary: Anti-corruption campaign, Belt and Road, term-limit abolition, Xinjiang repression and zero-COVID.

name: Chinese Accession to the WTO
summary: Entry into the World Trade Organization that accelerated China's export-led growth.

name: Belt and Road Initiative
summary: Global infrastructure and lending programme announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.

name: British Hong Kong
summary: Crown colony ceded in 1842 and leased in 1898 that became a global financial centre.

name: Handover of Hong Kong
summary: Transfer of sovereignty to China on 1 July 1997 under 'one country, two systems'.

name: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
summary: Autonomous Chinese territory whose freedoms narrowed after the 2019 protests and 2020 national security law.

name: Hong Kong Protests of 2019
summary: Mass movement against an extradition bill, answered by Beijing's national security law.

name: Portuguese Macau
summary: Oldest European settlement in East Asia, returned to China in 1999.

name: Macau Special Administrative Region
summary: Chinese special administrative region and the world's largest gambling centre.

name: Republic of China on Taiwan
summary: Nationalist government relocated to Taipei in 1949; now a democracy claimed by the PRC.

name: Japanese Taiwan
summary: Fifty years of Japanese colonial rule that industrialised the island.

name: February 28 Incident
summary: Nationalist suppression of a Taiwanese uprising, followed by the White Terror.

name: Taiwanese Martial Law Period
summary: Thirty-eight years of one-party Kuomintang rule under martial law and the White Terror.

name: Rule of Chiang Kai-shek
summary: Nationalist leader who unified China in 1928, lost the civil war and governed Taiwan until his death.

name: Taiwanese Democratisation
summary: Lifting of martial law, party competition and the first direct presidential election in 1996.

name: Taiwan Strait Crises
summary: Series of military confrontations between the PRC and Taiwan involving American intervention.

name: Dzungar Khanate
summary: Last great steppe empire, destroyed by the Qing in a campaign of near-annihilation.

name: Qing Mongolia
summary: Outer and Inner Mongolia under Qing administration through the Manchu-Mongol aristocratic system.

name: Bogd Khanate of Mongolia
summary: Theocratic Mongolian state under the Jebtsundamba Khutughtu after the Qing collapse.

name: Mongolian People's Republic
summary: Second communist state in the world, a Soviet satellite with purges of the Buddhist clergy.

name: Mongolia
summary: Democratic parliamentary republic since 1992 with a mining-based economy.

name: Late Joseon Dynasty
summary: Neo-Confucian kingdom that survived the Imjin and Manchu invasions and pursued isolation until forced open.

name: Imjin War
summary: Hideyoshi's two invasions of Korea, repelled with Ming aid and Admiral Yi Sun-sin's naval victories.

name: Korean Empire
summary: Gojong's proclaimed empire, which attempted reform before becoming a Japanese protectorate and colony.

name: Japanese Colonial Rule in Korea
summary: Thirty-five years of colonial rule with land expropriation, assimilation policy and wartime forced labour.

name: March First Movement
summary: Nationwide independence demonstrations suppressed with thousands killed.

name: Division of Korea
summary: American and Soviet occupation zones split at the 38th parallel, hardening into two states.

name: Republic of Korea
summary: South Korean state founded in 1948, which industrialised rapidly and democratised in 1987.

name: Democratic People's Republic of Korea
summary: Northern state under three generations of Kim family rule, nuclear-armed since 2006.

name: Korean War
summary: War begun by the North's invasion, drawing in UN and Chinese forces; an armistice, not a peace, ended fighting.

name: Rule of Kim Il-sung
summary: Founding leader who built the juche system and a hereditary personality cult.

name: Rule of Kim Jong-il
summary: Ruled through the 1990s famine and the first nuclear test, under 'military first' policy.

name: Rule of Kim Jong-un
summary: Third-generation leader who expanded the nuclear and missile programmes and met US and South Korean leaders.

name: North Korean Famine
summary: Famine after Soviet aid ended that killed hundreds of thousands.

name: Presidency of Syngman Rhee
summary: Authoritarian founding president, ousted by the April Revolution.

name: Rule of Park Chung-hee
summary: Military strongman who drove export-led industrialisation under the repressive Yushin system; assassinated in 1979.

name: Gwangju Uprising
summary: Pro-democracy revolt crushed by paratroopers under Chun Doo-hwan with hundreds killed.

name: June Democratic Struggle
summary: Mass protests that forced direct presidential elections and the end of military rule.

name: Miracle on the Han River
summary: Transformation from postwar poverty to an advanced industrial economy led by chaebol conglomerates.

name: Asian Financial Crisis
summary: Currency and banking collapse from Thailand to Korea and Indonesia, with IMF programmes and political upheaval.

name: Mughal Empire
summary: Timurid Muslim empire that ruled most of South Asia at its height and declined into a British-protected shell.

name: Reign of Babur
summary: Founder of the Mughal Empire, victorious at Panipat over the Delhi Sultanate.

name: Reign of Akbar
summary: Expanded and consolidated the empire, integrated Rajputs and pursued religious pluralism and the din-i ilahi.

name: Reign of Jahangir
summary: Reign of court painting, Nur Jahan's influence and the first English embassy.

name: Reign of Shah Jahan
summary: Builder of the Taj Mahal and Shahjahanabad, deposed by his son Aurangzeb.

name: Reign of Aurangzeb
summary: Expanded the empire to its greatest extent while exhausting it in the Deccan wars.

name: Maratha Empire
summary: Hindu power founded by Shivaji that displaced the Mughals across much of India before defeat by the British.

name: Reign of Shivaji
summary: Founder-king who built a Maratha state through guerrilla war against the Mughals and Bijapur.

name: Third Battle of Panipat
summary: Afghan victory over the Marathas that crippled the leading Indian power and eased British expansion.

name: Sikh Empire
summary: Ranjit Singh's Punjab state, which annexed Kashmir and Peshawar and fell in the Anglo-Sikh Wars.

name: Kingdom of Mysore
summary: South Indian state whose rulers Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan fought four wars against the British.

name: East India Company Rule in India
summary: Company government from Plassey to the Crown takeover, extended by conquest, subsidiary alliances and revenue farming.

name: Battle of Plassey
summary: Clive's victory in Bengal that began British territorial power in India.

name: Great Bengal Famine of 1770
summary: Famine under early Company rule that killed several million Bengalis.

name: Anglo-Mysore Wars
summary: Four wars ending with the death of Tipu Sultan at Seringapatam.

name: Anglo-Maratha Wars
summary: Three wars that destroyed Maratha power and made the Company paramount in India.

name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
summary: Mass revolt of sepoys and princes that ended Company rule and the Mughal dynasty.

name: British Raj
summary: Crown rule over India, Burma and adjacent territories, with railways, famines, nationalism and partition.

name: Founding of the Indian National Congress
summary: First all-India nationalist organisation, later the vehicle of the independence movement.

name: Partition of Bengal (1905)
summary: Curzon's division of Bengal, reversed after the swadeshi agitation it provoked.

name: All-India Muslim League
summary: Party founded in Dhaka that under Jinnah demanded and won Pakistan.

name: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
summary: British troops fired on a crowd in Amritsar, killing hundreds and radicalising Indian opinion.

name: Non-Cooperation Movement
summary: Gandhi's first mass satyagraha, boycotting British schools, courts and goods.

name: Salt March
summary: Gandhi's 385-kilometre march to Dandi against the salt tax, launching civil disobedience.

name: Quit India Movement
summary: Congress demand for immediate independence, met by mass arrests and repression.

name: Bengal Famine of 1943
summary: Wartime famine that killed some three million people in Bengal.

name: Partition of India
summary: Division into India and Pakistan on 15 August 1947, with up to two million deaths and 15 million displaced.

name: Dominion of India
summary: Independent India under the crown until the republican constitution took effect.

name: Republic of India
summary: World's largest democracy, a federal republic under the 1950 constitution and the most populous country since 2023.

name: Indian Constitution
summary: Ambedkar-led constitution effective 26 January 1950, abolishing untouchability and creating a secular federal republic.

name: Premiership of Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: Founding prime minister: planning, non-alignment, states reorganisation and the 1962 war with China.

name: Integration of the Princely States
summary: Accession of over 500 princely states, including Hyderabad's forcible annexation.

name: First Kashmir War
summary: War over Kashmir after the maharaja's accession to India, ending with the ceasefire line.

name: Sino-Indian War
summary: Chinese victory in the Himalayan border war that shattered Nehru's China policy.

name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
summary: Second war over Kashmir, ended by the Soviet-brokered Tashkent Declaration.

name: Premiership of Indira Gandhi
summary: Prime minister 1966-77 and 1980-84: bank nationalisation, the 1971 war, the Emergency and her assassination.

name: The Emergency
summary: Twenty-one months of suspended civil liberties, press censorship and forced sterilisation under Indira Gandhi.

name: Operation Blue Star
summary: Army assault on the Golden Temple against Sikh militants, followed by Indira Gandhi's assassination and anti-Sikh pogroms.

name: Indian Economic Liberalisation
summary: Balance-of-payments crisis reforms under Rao and Manmohan Singh that opened the economy.

name: Indian and Pakistani Nuclear Tests
summary: Pokhran-II and Chagai tests made both states declared nuclear powers.

name: Kargil War
summary: High-altitude conflict after Pakistani infiltration into Indian-held Kashmir.

name: Premiership of Narendra Modi
summary: BJP prime minister: demonetisation, GST, abrogation of Article 370 and Hindu-nationalist consolidation.

name: Dominion of Pakistan
summary: Independent Pakistan under the crown, founded by Jinnah as a homeland for South Asian Muslims.

name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan
summary: Republic since 1956, alternating between civilian and military rule, nuclear-armed since 1998.

name: Leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah
summary: Quaid-i-Azam and founder of Pakistan, its first governor-general.

name: Rule of Ayub Khan
summary: First military ruler: the Decade of Development, the 1965 war and Islamabad's construction.

name: Government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
summary: Populist leader who wrote the 1973 constitution and began the nuclear programme; overthrown and hanged.

name: Rule of Zia-ul-Haq
summary: Islamising military dictatorship that backed the Afghan mujahideen; died in an air crash.

name: Premierships of Benazir Bhutto
summary: First woman to lead a Muslim-majority state, twice prime minister; assassinated in 2007.

name: Rule of Pervez Musharraf
summary: Coup leader who allied with the US after 9/11 and resigned amid the lawyers' movement.

name: Bangladesh Liberation War
summary: East Pakistan's war of independence with Indian intervention, accompanied by genocide against Bengalis.

name: People's Republic of Bangladesh
summary: Independent since 1971, one of the world's most densely populated states and a garment-export power.

name: Leadership of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
summary: Founding leader assassinated with most of his family in a 1975 coup.

name: Premierships of Sheikh Hasina
summary: Prime minister 1996-2001 and 2009-24, whose long rule ended in a student uprising and her flight in 2024.

name: Bangladeshi Uprising of 2024
summary: Student-led protests over job quotas that toppled Sheikh Hasina's government.

name: British Ceylon
summary: Crown colony after the fall of Kandy, with plantation tea and Tamil labour migration.

name: Dominion of Ceylon and Sri Lanka
summary: Independent in 1948, renamed Sri Lanka as a republic in 1972 after decades of communal tension.

name: Sri Lankan Civil War
summary: Twenty-six-year war between the state and the Tamil Tigers ending in the LTTE's destruction.

name: Kingdom of Nepal
summary: Shah dynasty state unified by Prithvi Narayan Shah, long dominated by the Rana premiers.

name: Rana Regime
summary: Hereditary prime ministers who reduced the Shah kings to figureheads for a century.

name: Nepalese Civil War
summary: Maoist insurgency that killed some 17,000 and led to the monarchy's abolition.

name: Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal
summary: Republic declared in 2008 after the Maoist war and the 2001 royal massacre.

name: Kingdom of Bhutan
summary: Himalayan Wangchuck monarchy, constitutional since 2008 and known for Gross National Happiness.

name: Republic of Maldives
summary: Indian Ocean island state independent from Britain in 1965, a republic from 1968.

name: Durrani Empire
summary: Ahmad Shah Durrani's empire stretching from Mashhad to Delhi, the foundation of modern Afghanistan.

name: Anglo-Afghan Wars
summary: Three British wars that failed to control Afghanistan, which won full independence in 1919.

name: Kingdom of Afghanistan
summary: Monarchy under Amanullah, Nadir Shah and Zahir Shah, ended by Daoud's republican coup.

name: Saur Revolution
summary: Communist coup that installed the PDPA and triggered rural revolt and Soviet intervention.

name: Soviet-Afghan War
summary: Nine-year Soviet occupation opposed by US- and Pakistan-backed mujahideen, ending in withdrawal.

name: Afghan Civil War of the 1990s
summary: Factional war after Najibullah's fall, won largely by the Taliban from 1996.

name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (first period)
summary: Taliban rule imposing strict shari'a and sheltering al-Qaeda, ended by US-led intervention.

name: United States War in Afghanistan
summary: Twenty-year NATO-led war after 9/11, ending in Taliban restoration and Western withdrawal.

name: Islamic Republic of Afghanistan
summary: Western-backed republic under Karzai and Ghani that collapsed as US forces left.

name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (restored)
summary: Taliban government since August 2021, unrecognised and enforcing severe restrictions on women.

name: Later Le Dynasty and Trinh-Nguyen Division
summary: Nominal Le kings with real power split between the Trinh lords in the north and the Nguyen in the south.

name: Tay Son Dynasty
summary: Peasant-led regime that unified Vietnam briefly and repelled a Qing invasion.

name: Nguyen Dynasty
summary: Last Vietnamese imperial dynasty, based at Hue, reduced to figureheads under French rule.

name: French Indochina
summary: French federation of Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin, Cambodia and Laos, exploited for rice, rubber and taxes.

name: French Conquest of Vietnam
summary: Campaigns from Saigon to Tonkin that made Vietnam a French colony and protectorates.

name: Japanese Occupation of Indochina
summary: Japanese control alongside Vichy French administration, ending in the 1945 coup and Vietnamese famine.

name: Vietnamese August Revolution
summary: Viet Minh seizure of power and Ho Chi Minh's declaration of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

name: First Indochina War
summary: Viet Minh war against France that ended with Dien Bien Phu and the Geneva Accords.

name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
summary: Viet Minh victory over the French garrison that ended French rule in Indochina.

name: Geneva Accords
summary: Agreements partitioning Vietnam at the 17th parallel and recognising Laotian and Cambodian independence.

name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam
summary: Communist northern state under Ho Chi Minh, which won the war and unified the country in 1976.

name: Republic of Vietnam
summary: Anti-communist southern state under Diem then Thieu, which collapsed with the fall of Saigon.

name: Leadership of Ho Chi Minh
summary: Founder of Vietnamese communism and president of North Vietnam until his death.

name: Vietnam War
summary: War between North and South Vietnam with massive American involvement, ending in communist victory.

name: Tet Offensive
summary: Coordinated communist attacks that failed militarily but broke American public support for the war.

name: Fall of Saigon
summary: North Vietnamese capture of Saigon on 30 April 1975 ended the war.

name: Socialist Republic of Vietnam
summary: Unified communist state since 1976, market-reforming since doi moi in 1986.

name: Doi Moi
summary: Market-oriented reforms that transformed Vietnam into a fast-growing export economy.

name: French Protectorate of Cambodia
summary: Norodom's kingdom under French protection within Indochina.

name: Kingdom of Cambodia (1953-1970)
summary: Sihanouk's independent, neutralist kingdom, ended by Lon Nol's coup.

name: Khmer Republic
summary: US-aligned republic under Lon Nol, defeated by the Khmer Rouge.

name: Democratic Kampuchea
summary: Khmer Rouge regime under Pol Pot that emptied the cities and killed some 1.7 to 2 million people.

name: Cambodian Genocide
summary: Mass killing, starvation and forced labour under the Khmer Rouge, about a quarter of the population.

name: Vietnamese Intervention in Cambodia
summary: Vietnamese invasion that ousted the Khmer Rouge and installed the People's Republic of Kampuchea.

name: UN Transitional Authority in Cambodia
summary: UN administration that organised elections and restored the monarchy.

name: Kingdom of Cambodia
summary: Restored constitutional monarchy, dominated politically by Hun Sen and his family since 1985.

name: Kingdom of Laos
summary: Independent kingdom torn by civil war and the Vietnam War's spillover bombing.

name: Lao People's Democratic Republic
summary: Communist state proclaimed after the Pathet Lao victory, the world's most heavily bombed country per capita.

name: Laotian Civil War
summary: Pathet Lao and North Vietnamese struggle against royalists, with a massive covert US air campaign.

name: Toungoo Dynasty
summary: Burmese dynasty that briefly built Southeast Asia's largest empire under Bayinnaung.

name: Konbaung Dynasty
summary: Last Burmese dynasty, which invaded Siam and Assam and lost three wars to Britain.

name: Anglo-Burmese Wars
summary: Three wars ending in the annexation of all Burma to British India.

name: British Burma
summary: Province of British India until 1937 and then a separate colony, occupied by Japan in 1942-45.

name: Union of Burma and Myanmar
summary: Independent from Britain in 1948, under military rule for most of its history and renamed Myanmar in 1989.

name: Rule of Ne Win
summary: Coup leader whose Burmese Way to Socialism isolated and impoverished the country.

name: Burmese Uprising of 1988
summary: Nationwide pro-democracy protests crushed by the army, which then formed the SLORC junta.

name: Political Career of Aung San Suu Kyi
summary: Nobel laureate held under house arrest for 15 years, later state counsellor and detained again in 2021.

name: Rohingya Crisis
summary: Military campaigns that drove over 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh, alleged as genocide.

name: Myanmar Coup of 2021
summary: Military seizure of power that sparked nationwide armed resistance and civil war.

name: Late Ayutthaya Kingdom
summary: Siamese kingdom of great wealth and cosmopolitan trade, destroyed by the Burmese in 1767.

name: Thonburi Kingdom
summary: Taksin's brief reunification of Siam after the fall of Ayutthaya.

name: Chakri Dynasty
summary: Bangkok dynasty that preserved Siamese independence through the colonial era and still reigns.

name: Reign of Mongkut
summary: Rama IV opened Siam to Western trade and diplomacy while preserving sovereignty.

name: Reign of Chulalongkorn
summary: Rama V abolished slavery, modernised administration and ceded border lands to keep Siam independent.

name: Siamese Revolution of 1932
summary: Bloodless coup that ended absolute monarchy and created a constitutional system dominated by the military.

name: Kingdom of Thailand
summary: Constitutional monarchy renamed Thailand in 1939, with a modern history of frequent military coups.

name: Reign of Bhumibol Adulyadej
summary: Rama IX reigned seventy years, becoming a unifying symbol through repeated coups.

name: Reign of Vajiralongkorn
summary: Rama X, king since 2016, whose reign has seen youth protests over royal reform.

name: Portuguese Conquest of Malacca
summary: Albuquerque's capture of Malacca gave Portugal control of a key Asian trade chokepoint.

name: Straits Settlements
summary: British colony of Penang, Malacca and Singapore, the hub of colonial commerce in the region.

name: British Malaya
summary: Federated and unfederated Malay states under British protection, built on tin and rubber.

name: Malayan Emergency
summary: British counterinsurgency against the Malayan Communist Party using resettlement and 'new villages'.

name: Federation of Malaya
summary: Independent Malaya from 31 August 1957 under Tunku Abdul Rahman.

name: Malaysia
summary: Federation formed in 1963 with Sabah, Sarawak and briefly Singapore; a rotating elective monarchy.

name: Separation of Singapore from Malaysia
summary: Singapore was expelled from the federation and became an independent republic on 9 August 1965.

name: Republic of Singapore
summary: City-state that grew from an entrepot to a global financial hub under Lee Kuan Yew's People's Action Party.

name: Premiership of Lee Kuan Yew
summary: Founding prime minister for 31 years who built a developmental, one-party-dominant state.

name: Brunei Darussalam
summary: Oil-rich Malay Islamic sultanate fully independent from Britain in 1984.

name: Dutch East Indies
summary: Dutch colonial state built on the VOC's ruins, exploiting sugar, coffee, oil and the cultivation system.

name: Java War
summary: Diponegoro's revolt against Dutch rule, ending in his exile and the cultivation system.

name: Aceh War
summary: Long Dutch war to subdue the Aceh sultanate, one of the colonial era's most costly campaigns.

name: Indonesian National Awakening
summary: Rise of nationalist organisations from Budi Utomo to Sukarno's PNI and the 1928 Youth Pledge.

name: Japanese Occupation of the Dutch East Indies
summary: Three years of Japanese rule that destroyed Dutch authority and armed Indonesian nationalists.

name: Indonesian National Revolution
summary: Four-year struggle after the 17 August 1945 proclamation that forced Dutch recognition of independence.

name: Republic of Indonesia
summary: World's largest archipelagic state and largest Muslim-majority country, independent since 1945.

name: Presidency of Sukarno
summary: Founding president: Pancasila, Bandung Conference, Guided Democracy and confrontation with Malaysia.

name: Bandung Conference
summary: First large Asian-African conference, a founding moment of Third World solidarity and non-alignment.

name: Indonesian Mass Killings of 1965-66
summary: Army-led massacre of at least half a million alleged communists after a failed coup.

name: New Order
summary: Suharto's authoritarian developmental regime, ended by the Asian financial crisis and mass protest.

name: Reformasi
summary: Democratisation after Suharto's fall, with decentralisation and direct presidential elections.

name: Indonesian Occupation of East Timor
summary: Invasion and annexation after Portuguese withdrawal, with perhaps 100,000 to 200,000 deaths.

name: Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste
summary: Independent in 2002 after a UN-run referendum and transitional administration.

name: Spanish Philippines
summary: Three centuries of Spanish rule administered from Mexico, with the Manila galleon trade and Catholic conversion.

name: Magellan's Arrival in the Philippines
summary: First European contact and Magellan's death at Mactan during the first circumnavigation.

name: Philippine Revolution
summary: Katipunan revolt under Bonifacio and Aguinaldo that ended Spanish rule.

name: First Philippine Republic
summary: Aguinaldo's Malolos republic, suppressed in the Philippine-American War.

name: Philippine-American War
summary: American conquest of the islands, with an estimated 200,000 or more Filipino civilian deaths.

name: American Colonial Philippines
summary: US colonial rule with public schooling and English, moving to Commonwealth status in 1935.

name: Commonwealth of the Philippines
summary: Transitional self-government under Manuel Quezon, interrupted by Japanese occupation.

name: Philippine Independence
summary: The United States granted independence on 4 July 1946.

name: Republic of the Philippines
summary: Southeast Asian republic independent since 1946, with the Marcos dictatorship and People Power in its history.

name: Marcos Regime
summary: Ferdinand Marcos ruled 21 years, including 14 under martial law with plunder and repression.

name: People Power Revolution
summary: Four days of mass non-violent protest that ousted Marcos and installed Corazon Aquino.

name: Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte
summary: Presidency defined by a lethal anti-drug campaign and pivot toward China.

name: Association of Southeast Asian Nations
summary: Regional organisation founded in Bangkok, now ten member states pursuing economic and security cooperation.

name: Ottoman Empire (Early Modern)
summary: Height of Ottoman power from Selim I's conquests to the Treaty of Karlowitz, spanning three continents.

name: Reign of Selim I
summary: Conquered the Mamluk sultanate and the Hejaz, bringing the caliphate and holy cities under Ottoman rule.

name: Reign of Suleiman the Magnificent
summary: Longest-reigning sultan: conquest of Belgrade, Rhodes and Hungary, legal codification and the siege of Vienna.

name: Battle of Lepanto
summary: Holy League naval victory over the Ottoman fleet that ended the myth of Ottoman invincibility at sea.

name: Sultanate of Women
summary: Period when imperial mothers and consorts exercised great political power in the Ottoman court.

name: Treaty of Karlowitz
summary: First treaty in which the Ottomans ceded major territory, giving Hungary to the Habsburgs.

name: Ottoman Decline and Reform
summary: Territorial losses to Russia and Austria, Janissary revolts, and the reforming reigns of Selim III and Mahmud II.

name: Reign of Mahmud II
summary: Destroyed the Janissaries in 1826 and began sweeping military and administrative Westernisation.

name: Tanzimat
summary: Reform era of legal equality, codified law, conscription and centralisation.

name: First Ottoman Constitutional Era
summary: Brief constitutional government under the 1876 Kanun-i Esasi, suspended by Abdulhamid II.

name: Reign of Abdulhamid II
summary: Autocratic sultan of railways and pan-Islamism who suspended parliament and was deposed by the Young Turks.

name: Young Turk Revolution
summary: Committee of Union and Progress forced the restoration of the constitution and parliament.

name: Ottoman Entry into the First World War
summary: Alliance with Germany brought campaigns at Gallipoli, in Mesopotamia, the Caucasus and Palestine.

name: Gallipoli Campaign
summary: Allied failure to force the Dardanelles, a formative event for Turkish, Australian and New Zealand identity.

name: Armenian Genocide
summary: Systematic deportation and killing of about 1.5 million Armenians, alongside Assyrians and Greeks.

name: Arab Revolt
summary: Hashemite rising against Ottoman rule, encouraged by Britain and aided by T. E. Lawrence.

name: Sykes-Picot Agreement
summary: Secret Anglo-French plan to divide Ottoman Arab lands, the basis of later mandate borders.

name: Treaty of Sevres
summary: Punitive partition treaty rejected by the Turkish nationalists and superseded by Lausanne.

name: Turkish War of Independence
summary: Kemal's nationalist campaign against Greek, Armenian and French forces that saved Anatolian sovereignty.

name: Abolition of the Ottoman Sultanate and Caliphate
summary: The sultanate ended in 1922 and the caliphate in 1924, closing six centuries of Ottoman rule.

name: Treaty of Lausanne
summary: Settlement recognising the Turkish republic's borders and mandating population exchange with Greece.

name: Republic of Turkey
summary: Secular republic founded by Ataturk on 29 October 1923, a NATO member since 1952.

name: Presidency of Mustafa Kemal Ataturk
summary: Founding president who abolished the caliphate, latinised the alphabet, secularised law and enfranchised women.

name: Presidency of Ismet Inonu
summary: Kept Turkey neutral in the Second World War and permitted the transition to multiparty democracy.

name: Turkish Military Coups
summary: Interventions in 1960, 1971, 1980 and 1997 that repeatedly reset Turkish politics.

name: Turkish Invasion of Cyprus
summary: Turkish intervention after a Greek-backed coup, dividing the island and creating a northern Turkish entity.

name: Erdogan Era
summary: Prime minister then president since 2003: economic growth, Islamic conservatism, the 2016 coup attempt and executive presidency.

name: Turkish Coup Attempt of 2016
summary: Failed military putsch followed by mass purges and a state of emergency.

name: Republic of Cyprus
summary: Independent from Britain in 1960, de facto divided since 1974 and an EU member since 2004.

name: Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
summary: Self-declared state recognised only by Turkey.

name: Safavid Empire
summary: Dynasty that made Twelver Shi'ism Iran's state religion and built Isfahan as an imperial capital.

name: Reign of Shah Abbas I
summary: Reformed the army, retook lands from the Ottomans and Uzbeks, and rebuilt Isfahan.

name: Afsharid Dynasty
summary: Nader Shah's short-lived empire, which sacked Delhi in 1739 and collapsed after his assassination.

name: Zand Dynasty
summary: Karim Khan's relatively peaceful regime based at Shiraz.

name: Qajar Dynasty
summary: Dynasty that lost the Caucasus to Russia, granted foreign concessions and faced the Constitutional Revolution.

name: Russo-Persian Wars
summary: Wars ending in the treaties of Gulistan and Turkmenchay, which ceded the Caucasus to Russia.

name: Tobacco Protest
summary: Nationwide boycott led by clerics that forced cancellation of a British tobacco monopoly.

name: Persian Constitutional Revolution
summary: Movement that won a constitution and the first Majlis, then was undermined by royal and foreign intervention.

name: Anglo-Russian Convention
summary: Agreement dividing Persia into Russian and British spheres of influence.

name: Discovery of Oil in Persia
summary: Masjed Soleyman strike led to the Anglo-Persian Oil Company and a century of oil politics.

name: Pahlavi Dynasty
summary: Two shahs who modernised, secularised and centralised Iran until the Islamic Revolution.

name: Reign of Reza Shah Pahlavi
summary: Army officer turned shah who built railways, unveiled women and was deposed by the Allies in 1941.

name: Anglo-Soviet Invasion of Iran
summary: Allied occupation to secure oil and a supply corridor to the USSR, forcing Reza Shah's abdication.

name: Reign of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
summary: Last shah: oil nationalisation crisis, the 1953 coup, White Revolution, SAVAK repression and revolution.

name: Iranian Oil Nationalisation
summary: Mosaddegh's nationalisation of the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company, met by boycott and covert action.

name: Iranian Coup of 1953
summary: CIA and MI6 operation that removed Prime Minister Mosaddegh and restored the shah's power.

name: White Revolution
summary: Shah's programme of land reform, literacy and women's suffrage that also displaced rural populations.

name: Iranian Revolution
summary: Mass movement that overthrew the shah and established an Islamic republic under Khomeini.

name: Islamic Republic of Iran
summary: Theocratic republic with a supreme leader and elected institutions, in confrontation with the West since 1979.

name: Iran Hostage Crisis
summary: 444-day seizure of the US embassy in Tehran that severed relations with Washington.

name: Leadership of Ruhollah Khomeini
summary: Founder and first supreme leader, who institutionalised clerical rule and led the war with Iraq.

name: Iran-Iraq War
summary: Eight-year war of attrition with chemical weapons and about a million casualties, ending in stalemate.

name: Leadership of Ali Khamenei
summary: Supreme leader since 1989, presiding over nuclear disputes, sanctions and protest movements.

name: Iranian Green Movement
summary: Mass protests against a disputed presidential election, suppressed by security forces.

name: Iran Nuclear Deal
summary: JCPOA limiting Iran's nuclear programme for sanctions relief, abandoned by the United States in 2018.

name: Mahsa Amini Protests
summary: Nationwide 'Woman, Life, Freedom' uprising after a young woman's death in morality police custody.

name: Ottoman Syria and the Levant
summary: Four centuries of Ottoman provincial rule over Syria, Lebanon, Palestine and Transjordan.

name: Emirate of Mount Lebanon
summary: Autonomous Druze and Maronite emirate under Ottoman suzerainty, notably under Fakhr al-Din II.

name: Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate
summary: Autonomous Christian-governed Ottoman province created after the 1860 civil war under European pressure.

name: Mandatory Palestine
summary: British League of Nations mandate under the Balfour Declaration's terms, ending in war and partition.

name: Balfour Declaration
summary: British pledge to favour a Jewish national home in Palestine while protecting non-Jewish rights.

name: Zionist Movement
summary: Political movement founded at Basel by Herzl to establish a Jewish state, realised in 1948.

name: Arab Revolt in Palestine
summary: Palestinian rebellion against British rule and Jewish immigration, suppressed with heavy casualties.

name: United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine
summary: Resolution 181 recommended Jewish and Arab states with international status for Jerusalem.

name: State of Israel
summary: Jewish state declared on 14 May 1948, which has fought repeated wars with its neighbours and Palestinians.

name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
summary: War following Israel's declaration, ending in armistice lines and the displacement of most Palestinian Arabs.

name: Nakba
summary: Expulsion and flight of about 750,000 Palestinians and the destruction of hundreds of villages.

name: Premiership of David Ben-Gurion
summary: Founding prime minister who built state institutions, absorbed mass immigration and led the 1956 Sinai campaign.

name: Suez Crisis
summary: British, French and Israeli attack on Egypt after Nasser nationalised the canal, reversed by US and Soviet pressure.

name: Six-Day War
summary: Israeli victory over Egypt, Jordan and Syria that took Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, Jerusalem and the Golan.

name: Yom Kippur War
summary: Egyptian and Syrian surprise attack on Israel that led to the oil embargo and eventually to peace talks.

name: Camp David Accords
summary: Egyptian-Israeli peace brokered by Carter, returning Sinai to Egypt; Sadat was assassinated in 1981.

name: Lebanese Civil War
summary: Fifteen-year multi-sided war with Syrian and Israeli intervention, ending in the Taif Agreement.

name: Israeli Invasion of Lebanon
summary: Invasion to expel the PLO, the siege of Beirut and the Sabra and Shatila massacre.

name: Palestine Liberation Organization
summary: Umbrella national movement led by Yasser Arafat from 1969, recognised as the Palestinian representative.

name: First Intifada
summary: Palestinian mass uprising in the occupied territories, ended by the Oslo process.

name: Oslo Accords
summary: Israeli-Palestinian agreements creating the Palestinian Authority and mutual recognition.

name: Palestinian Authority
summary: Interim self-governing body in the West Bank and, until 2007, Gaza.

name: Second Intifada
summary: Violent uprising with suicide bombings and Israeli reoccupation, followed by the separation barrier.

name: Israeli Disengagement from Gaza
summary: Israel withdrew settlers and soldiers from Gaza, which Hamas took over in 2007.

name: State of Palestine
summary: Declared in 1988 and recognised by most UN members; a UN observer state since 2012.

name: Gaza War
summary: War following the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023, with devastating destruction and casualties in Gaza.

name: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
summary: French League of Nations mandate that created the borders of modern Syria and Lebanon.

name: Lebanese Republic
summary: Independent confessional republic, shaped by civil war, Syrian tutelage and economic collapse.

name: Syrian Arab Republic
summary: Independent from France in 1946; Ba'athist from 1963, ruled by the Assads from 1970 to 2024.

name: United Arab Republic
summary: Short-lived union of Egypt and Syria under Nasser, dissolved by a Syrian coup.

name: Rule of Hafez al-Assad
summary: Thirty years of Ba'athist Alawite-led authoritarian rule, including the 1982 Hama massacre.

name: Rule of Bashar al-Assad
summary: Presidency that met the 2011 uprising with war, chemical attacks and displacement, ending in his flight in December 2024.

name: Syrian Civil War
summary: Uprising turned multi-sided war with Russian, Iranian, Turkish and US involvement and over half a million dead.

name: Fall of the Assad Regime
summary: Rebel offensive that captured Damascus in December 2024 and ended 54 years of Assad family rule.

name: British Mandate for Mesopotamia
summary: British mandate over Iraq established after the Ottoman collapse, resisted in the 1920 revolt.

name: Kingdom of Iraq
summary: Hashemite kingdom independent from 1932, overthrown in the bloody 1958 revolution.

name: Republic of Iraq
summary: Republic since 1958: Ba'athist rule, three wars, occupation and a federal constitution since 2005.

name: Rule of Saddam Hussein
summary: Ba'athist dictator: war with Iran, gassing of Kurds, invasion of Kuwait and overthrow by US-led invasion.

name: Gulf War
summary: US-led coalition expelled Iraq from Kuwait after its August 1990 invasion.

name: Iraq War
summary: US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein, followed by insurgency, sectarian civil war and occupation.

name: Islamic State Caliphate
summary: Jihadist proto-state that seized Mosul and Raqqa before being destroyed by coalition and local forces.

name: Kurdistan Region of Iraq
summary: Autonomous Kurdish region established under no-fly-zone protection and constitutionally recognised in 2005.

name: The Kurdish Question
summary: Statelessness of the Kurds after Sevres, with insurgencies and autonomy struggles in Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

name: Emirate of Transjordan
summary: British-mandated Hashemite emirate under Abdullah I, independent as a kingdom in 1946.

name: Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
summary: Hashemite monarchy independent in 1946, host to large Palestinian refugee populations.

name: Reign of King Hussein of Jordan
summary: Forty-six-year reign through the 1967 war, Black September and peace with Israel in 1994.

name: Emirate of Diriyah
summary: First Saudi state, founded on the alliance of Muhammad ibn Saud and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, crushed by Egypt.

name: Emirate of Nejd
summary: Second Saudi state, based at Riyadh, overthrown by the Rashidis.

name: Unification of Saudi Arabia
summary: Ibn Saud's campaigns from the recapture of Riyadh to the proclamation of the kingdom in 1932.

name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
summary: Absolute monarchy guarding Mecca and Medina, transformed by the world's largest conventional oil reserves.

name: Discovery of Saudi Oil
summary: Dammam strike that made Saudi Arabia the centre of world oil and founded Aramco.

name: Reign of King Faisal
summary: Modernising king who led the 1973 oil embargo; assassinated by a nephew.

name: Reign of King Fahd
summary: King during the Gulf War, when US troops were stationed in the kingdom, and the Basic Law of 1992.

name: Reign of King Abdullah
summary: Cautious reformer who expanded education and faced the Arab Spring.

name: Rule of Mohammed bin Salman
summary: Crown prince driving Vision 2030 reforms, the Yemen war and a crackdown on dissent.

name: Seizure of the Grand Mosque
summary: Two-week takeover of the Kaaba compound by militants, after which the kingdom hardened religious policy.

name: State of Kuwait
summary: Oil-rich Gulf emirate independent from Britain in 1961, occupied by Iraq in 1990-91.

name: Kingdom of Bahrain
summary: Gulf island state independent in 1971 and a kingdom since 2002, host to the US Fifth Fleet.

name: State of Qatar
summary: Gas-rich emirate independent in 1971, home to Al Jazeera and host of the 2022 World Cup.

name: United Arab Emirates
summary: Federation of seven emirates formed on British withdrawal, now a global trade and finance hub.

name: Sultanate of Oman
summary: Al Bu Said sultanate that once ruled Zanzibar, modernised after Sultan Qaboos took power in 1970.

name: Dhofar Rebellion
summary: Leftist insurgency in southern Oman defeated with British and Iranian help.

name: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen
summary: Zaydi imamate in North Yemen, overthrown in the 1962 revolution.

name: People's Democratic Republic of Yemen
summary: Marxist state based at Aden after British withdrawal, merged with the north in 1990.

name: Republic of Yemen
summary: Unified in 1990, since 2014 divided by civil war and Saudi-led intervention.

name: Yemeni Civil War
summary: Houthi takeover of Sanaa and Saudi-led intervention producing a severe humanitarian crisis.

name: Arab Spring
summary: Wave of uprisings from Tunisia to Bahrain that toppled four rulers and triggered wars in Libya, Syria and Yemen.

name: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
summary: Cartel founded in Baghdad that reshaped global energy politics, notably in the 1973 embargo.

name: 1973 Oil Crisis
summary: Arab oil embargo that quadrupled prices, ending the postwar boom and reshaping energy policy.

name: Arab League
summary: Regional organisation of Arab states founded in Cairo in 1945.

name: Gulf Cooperation Council
summary: Six-member Gulf political and economic union founded in 1981.

name: Abraham Accords
summary: Normalisation agreements between Israel and the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan.

name: Scramble for Africa
summary: European powers partitioned almost the whole continent in three decades of conquest and treaty-making.

name: Berlin Conference
summary: Fourteen powers set rules for African colonisation and recognised Leopold II's Congo Free State.

name: British Colonial Africa
summary: British colonies and protectorates from the Cape to Egypt, decolonised mainly between 1956 and 1980.

name: French Colonial Africa
summary: French West and Equatorial Africa plus the Maghreb, mostly independent in 1960 and Algeria in 1962.

name: German Colonial Africa
summary: Togo, Kamerun, South West Africa and East Africa, lost as mandates after the First World War.

name: Italian Colonial Africa
summary: Eritrea, Somalia, Libya and briefly Ethiopia, lost during the Second World War.

name: Belgian Colonial Africa
summary: Belgian Congo plus Ruanda-Urundi, decolonised abruptly in 1960-62.

name: Portuguese Colonial Africa
summary: Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde and Sao Tome, held until the Carnation Revolution.

name: Decolonisation of Africa
summary: Independence of more than fifty states, from Libya in 1951 to South Africa's democratic transition in 1994.

name: Year of Africa
summary: Seventeen African countries became independent in 1960, transforming the United Nations.

name: Organisation of African Unity
summary: Pan-African body founded in Addis Ababa that upheld colonial borders and backed liberation movements.

name: African Union
summary: Continental organisation succeeding the OAU, with a Peace and Security Council and free-trade area.

name: Pan-Africanism
summary: Movement for African unity and diaspora solidarity from the early congresses to Nkrumah and the AU.

name: Indian Ocean and Trans-Saharan Slave Trades
summary: Long-running slave trades across the Sahara and Indian Ocean, ended by gradual abolition and colonial rule.

name: Ottoman Egypt
summary: Ottoman province governed by Mamluk-Ottoman elites, briefly occupied by Napoleon in 1798.

name: French Invasion of Egypt
summary: Napoleon's campaign that shattered Mamluk power, produced the Description de l'Egypte and ended in British-Ottoman victory.

name: Rule of Muhammad Ali of Egypt
summary: Albanian-Ottoman officer who massacred the Mamluks and built a modern army, industry and cotton economy.

name: Khedivate of Egypt
summary: Autonomous Ottoman khedivate that built the Suez Canal, went bankrupt and fell under British control.

name: Opening of the Suez Canal
summary: Waterway linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea, transforming global trade and Egypt's strategic value.

name: British Occupation of Egypt
summary: Occupation after the Urabi revolt, formalised as a protectorate in 1914 and ended by the 1956 evacuation.

name: Kingdom of Egypt
summary: Nominally independent monarchy under Fuad I and Farouk, dominated by Britain and ended by revolution.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 1952
summary: Free Officers' coup that deposed Farouk and brought Nasser to power.

name: Arab Republic of Egypt
summary: Republic since 1953: Nasserism, wars with Israel, Sadat's peace, Mubarak's rule and the 2011 revolution.

name: Rule of Gamal Abdel Nasser
summary: Pan-Arab leader who nationalised the canal, built the Aswan High Dam and lost the 1967 war.

name: Aswan High Dam
summary: Soviet-aided dam that controlled the Nile flood, created Lake Nasser and displaced Nubian communities.

name: Presidency of Anwar Sadat
summary: Launched the 1973 war, expelled Soviet advisers, made peace with Israel and was assassinated in 1981.

name: Presidency of Hosni Mubarak
summary: Thirty years of authoritarian stability, ended by the Tahrir Square uprising.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 2011
summary: Eighteen days of protest centred on Tahrir Square that forced Mubarak's resignation.

name: Presidency of Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
summary: Army chief who led the 2013 coup and has ruled since 2014 with severe restrictions on dissent.

name: Regency of Algiers
summary: Ottoman-aligned corsair state on the Barbary coast, conquered by France in 1830.

name: French Conquest of Algeria
summary: Long, violent conquest and settlement, resisted by Abd al-Qadir and Kabyle revolts.

name: French Algeria
summary: Departments of France with a large settler population, ended by the war of independence.

name: Algerian War of Independence
summary: Eight-year FLN insurgency and French counterinsurgency that killed hundreds of thousands and toppled the Fourth Republic.

name: Battle of Algiers
summary: Urban campaign of bombings and systematic French torture that became emblematic of the war.

name: People's Democratic Republic of Algeria
summary: Independent from France in 1962, hydrocarbon-dependent and shaped by FLN rule and the 1990s civil war.

name: Algerian Civil War
summary: War between the state and Islamist insurgents after cancelled elections, with about 150,000 to 200,000 dead.

name: Alaouite Sultanate of Morocco
summary: Sharifian dynasty that has ruled Morocco since the 17th century, surviving colonial protectorate.

name: French and Spanish Protectorates in Morocco
summary: Treaty of Fez protectorate with a Spanish zone, resisted in the Rif War and ended in 1956.

name: Rif War
summary: Abd el-Krim's republic defeated Spanish armies before falling to a Franco-Spanish offensive.

name: Kingdom of Morocco
summary: Independent monarchy since 1956 under Mohammed V, Hassan II and Mohammed VI.

name: Western Sahara Conflict
summary: Moroccan annexation after Spanish withdrawal, contested by the Polisario Front and a stalled UN referendum.

name: Green March
summary: Mass Moroccan civilian march into Spanish Sahara that secured Moroccan control.

name: Husainid Beylik of Tunis
summary: Dynasty that ruled Tunisia under Ottoman then French suzerainty until the republic.

name: French Protectorate of Tunisia
summary: Protectorate established by the Treaty of Bardo, ended by Neo Destour's independence campaign.

name: Republic of Tunisia
summary: Independent republic under Bourguiba then Ben Ali, birthplace of the Arab Spring.

name: Rule of Habib Bourguiba
summary: Founding president who secularised law and advanced women's rights before being deposed for senility.

name: Tunisian Revolution
summary: Protests after Mohamed Bouazizi's self-immolation that ousted Ben Ali and began the Arab Spring.

name: Ottoman Tripolitania
summary: Ottoman and Karamanli rule over the Libyan coast, ended by the Italian invasion.

name: Italian Libya
summary: Italian colony whose pacification killed a large share of the Cyrenaican population.

name: Kingdom of Libya
summary: Senussi monarchy under Idris I, independent by UN resolution and transformed by oil.

name: Rule of Muammar Gaddafi
summary: Forty-two years of idiosyncratic rule under the Jamahiriya, ended by uprising and NATO intervention.

name: Libyan Civil Wars
summary: Uprising and NATO campaign that killed Gaddafi, followed by a decade of rival governments and militias.

name: Mahdist State
summary: Islamic state founded after the fall of Khartoum, destroyed by Kitchener at Omdurman.

name: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
summary: Condominium administered largely by Britain, which governed the south separately.

name: Republic of the Sudan
summary: Independent in 1956, marked by two civil wars, Darfur, Bashir's rule and renewed war from 2023.

name: First Sudanese Civil War
summary: North-south conflict ended by the Addis Ababa Agreement's autonomy for the south.

name: Second Sudanese Civil War
summary: Twenty-two-year war with the SPLA that killed some two million and ended in a peace deal.

name: Darfur Conflict
summary: Government and Janjaweed campaign against Darfuri rebels and civilians, described as genocide.

name: Rule of Omar al-Bashir
summary: Islamist military ruler indicted by the ICC, overthrown by protests and the army in 2019.

name: Republic of South Sudan
summary: World's newest widely recognised state, independent by referendum in 2011 and soon at civil war.

name: Sudanese Civil War of 2023
summary: War between the army and the Rapid Support Forces that produced the world's largest displacement crisis.

name: Fall of the Songhai Empire
summary: Moroccan musketeers defeated Songhai at Tondibi, ending the last great Sahelian empire.

name: Kingdom of Benin (late)
summary: Powerful Edo kingdom famed for its bronzes, sacked and looted by a British punitive expedition in 1897.

name: Oyo Empire
summary: Yoruba cavalry empire that dominated the slave-trading coast before collapsing into civil wars.

name: Asante Empire
summary: Akan gold and trading empire centred on Kumasi, annexed by Britain after five wars.

name: Kingdom of Dahomey
summary: West African kingdom with its famous women's regiments, conquered by France in the 1890s.

name: Sokoto Caliphate
summary: Vast Fulani state founded by Usman dan Fodio's jihad, defeated by Britain and incorporated as an emirate system.

name: Gold Coast
summary: British colony built on gold, cocoa and the conquest of Asante, first in sub-Saharan Africa to independence.

name: Republic of Ghana
summary: First sub-Saharan colony to gain independence, on 6 March 1957, under Kwame Nkrumah.

name: Rule of Kwame Nkrumah
summary: Pan-Africanist founding leader who built the Akosombo Dam and was overthrown by a coup in 1966.

name: Colonial Nigeria
summary: British protectorates amalgamated in 1914 and ruled through indirect rule over emirs and chiefs.

name: Federal Republic of Nigeria
summary: Africa's most populous state, independent in 1960, oil-rich and shaped by civil war and military rule.

name: Nigerian Civil War
summary: Biafra's secession and blockade, which killed one to two million people, mostly by starvation.

name: Nigerian Military Rule
summary: Nearly three decades of coups and juntas, including Abacha's dictatorship, ending with the Fourth Republic.

name: Nigerian Fourth Republic
summary: Civilian democracy since 1999, contending with Boko Haram, oil-delta conflict and rapid population growth.

name: Boko Haram Insurgency
summary: Jihadist conflict in the northeast with mass abductions and millions displaced across the Lake Chad basin.

name: Republic of Senegal
summary: West African republic independent in 1960, notable for stable civilian rule and Leopold Senghor's presidency.

name: Mali Federation
summary: Short-lived union of Senegal and French Sudan that split within months of independence.

name: Republic of Mali
summary: Sahelian republic independent in 1960, since 2012 facing jihadist insurgency and coups.

name: Mali War
summary: Tuareg and jihadist rebellion, French intervention and successive military coups.

name: Republic of Cote d'Ivoire
summary: Cocoa-exporting republic independent in 1960 under Houphouet-Boigny, later split by civil war.

name: Republic of Guinea
summary: Only French African colony to reject the 1958 community, independent under Sekou Toure.

name: Republic of Guinea-Bissau
summary: Independent after Amilcar Cabral's PAIGC war against Portugal.

name: Republic of Cabo Verde
summary: Atlantic island republic independent from Portugal in 1975, a stable multiparty democracy.

name: Burkina Faso
summary: Independent as Upper Volta in 1960, renamed by Thomas Sankara in 1984, now facing jihadist war and coups.

name: Rule of Thomas Sankara
summary: Revolutionary leader of literacy, vaccination and anti-imperial rhetoric, assassinated in 1987.

name: Republic of Niger
summary: Sahelian uranium-producing republic independent in 1960, with a 2023 coup ending civilian rule.

name: Republic of Benin
summary: Independent as Dahomey in 1960, Marxist from 1975 to 1990 and a pioneer of African democratic transition.

name: Togolese Republic
summary: Former German then French territory independent in 1960, ruled by the Gnassingbe family since 1967.

name: Republic of Sierra Leone
summary: Founded as a settlement for freed slaves, independent in 1961 and scarred by a diamond-fuelled civil war.

name: Sierra Leone Civil War
summary: Brutal war involving the RUF and blood diamonds, ended by British and UN intervention.

name: Republic of Liberia
