summary: Founded by freed American slaves and independent from 1847, later devastated by two civil wars.

name: Liberian Civil Wars
summary: Two wars involving Charles Taylor that killed about 250,000 and destabilised the region.

name: Republic of The Gambia
summary: Small riverine state independent in 1965, ruled by Yahya Jammeh from 1994 to 2017.

name: Islamic Republic of Mauritania
summary: Saharan republic independent in 1960, which formally abolished slavery only in 1981.

name: Kingdom of Kongo
summary: Christianised Central African kingdom that traded with Portugal and declined under the slave trade.

name: Congo Free State
summary: Leopold II's personal colony whose rubber regime caused mass death and international scandal.

name: Belgian Congo
summary: Belgian state colony exploited for copper, rubber and uranium, decolonised abruptly in 1960.

name: Congo Crisis
summary: Post-independence collapse: Katangese secession, Lumumba's murder, UN intervention and Mobutu's rise.

name: Rule of Mobutu Sese Seko
summary: Thirty-two years of kleptocratic rule over the country he renamed Zaire.

name: Republic of Zaire
summary: Mobutu's renamed state, ended by Kabila's rebellion in the First Congo War.

name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
summary: Vast mineral-rich state renamed in 1997, still troubled by conflict in its eastern provinces.

name: First Congo War
summary: Rwandan- and Ugandan-backed rebellion that overthrew Mobutu.

name: Second Congo War
summary: Africa's world war, involving nine countries and causing millions of deaths, mostly from disease and hunger.

name: Republic of the Congo
summary: Former French Congo independent in 1960, oil-exporting and long ruled by Denis Sassou Nguesso.

name: Kingdom of Rwanda
summary: Tutsi-led monarchy that colonial rule reinforced before the 1959 Hutu revolution abolished it.

name: Ruanda-Urundi
summary: Belgian mandate then trust territory that hardened Hutu-Tutsi categories through identity cards.

name: Republic of Rwanda
summary: Independent in 1962, site of the 1994 genocide and since then of state-led reconstruction under Paul Kagame.

name: Rwandan Civil War
summary: RPF invasion and war that led to the Arusha Accords and then to genocide.

name: Rwandan Genocide
summary: Roughly 800,000 to one million Tutsi and moderate Hutu killed in about a hundred days.

name: Rule of Paul Kagame
summary: RPF leader, president since 2000, credited with development and criticised for authoritarianism.

name: Republic of Burundi
summary: Independent in 1962, marked by mass killings in 1972 and 1993 and a long civil war.

name: Kingdom of Buganda
summary: Powerful lacustrine kingdom, the core of the Uganda Protectorate, abolished in 1966 and restored in 1993.

name: Uganda Protectorate
summary: British protectorate ruled indirectly through Buganda's institutions.

name: Republic of Uganda
summary: Independent in 1962, ravaged under Amin and Obote, ruled by Yoweri Museveni since 1986.

name: Rule of Idi Amin
summary: Brutal dictatorship that expelled Uganda's Asians and killed hundreds of thousands, ended by Tanzanian invasion.

name: East Africa Protectorate and Kenya Colony
summary: British colony of settler highlands, the Uganda railway and land alienation from the Kikuyu and Maasai.

name: Mau Mau Uprising
summary: Kikuyu-led rebellion met by mass detention camps and emergency rule, hastening independence.

name: Republic of Kenya
summary: Independent in 1963 under Jomo Kenyatta, later multiparty and shaped by the 2007-08 election violence.

name: Rule of Jomo Kenyatta
summary: Founding leader who pursued capitalist development and centralised power in KANU.

name: Rule of Daniel arap Moi
summary: Twenty-four-year one-party then multiparty presidency marked by patronage and repression.

name: Sultanate of Zanzibar
summary: Omani-derived clove and slave-trading sultanate, a British protectorate from 1890, overthrown in the 1964 revolution.

name: German East Africa
summary: German colony covering Tanganyika, Rwanda and Burundi, site of the Maji Maji rebellion.

name: Maji Maji Rebellion
summary: Mass revolt against German rule crushed by famine tactics with perhaps 250,000 deaths.

name: Tanganyika
summary: British mandate then trust territory, independent in 1961 and united with Zanzibar in 1964.

name: United Republic of Tanzania
summary: Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, shaped by Nyerere's ujamaa socialism and later liberalisation.

name: Rule of Julius Nyerere
summary: Founding president whose ujamaa villagisation failed economically but built national unity and literacy.

name: Ethiopian Empire
summary: Christian Solomonic empire that survived European conquest and was abolished by the Derg.

name: Reign of Tewodros II
summary: Reunified Ethiopia after the era of princes; died resisting a British expedition at Magdala.

name: Reign of Menelik II
summary: Expanded the empire southward, founded Addis Ababa and defeated Italy at Adwa.

name: Battle of Adwa
summary: Ethiopian defeat of an Italian army, the only decisive African victory over a European colonial power.

name: Reign of Haile Selassie
summary: Last emperor: exile under Italian occupation, postwar modernisation, OAU founding and deposition by famine and revolt.

name: Italian Occupation of Ethiopia
summary: Five years of Italian East Africa rule with poison gas and reprisals, ended by British and Ethiopian forces.

name: Derg
summary: Marxist military junta under Mengistu: Red Terror, famine and war with Eritrea and Somalia.

name: Ethiopian Famine of 1983-85
summary: Drought and war famine that killed several hundred thousand and prompted global relief campaigns.

name: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
summary: Ethnic-federal republic established after the Derg's fall, later shaken by the Tigray war.

name: Eritrean War of Independence
summary: Thirty-year struggle against Ethiopian rule won by the EPLF in 1991.

name: State of Eritrea
summary: Independent by referendum in 1993, ruled since by Isaias Afwerki without elections.

name: Eritrean-Ethiopian War
summary: Border war over Badme that killed tens of thousands and froze relations until 2018.

name: Tigray War
summary: Federal and Eritrean campaign against Tigray's regional government, with mass atrocities and famine conditions.

name: Somali Republic
summary: Union of British and Italian Somaliland in 1960, collapsed into statelessness after 1991.

name: Rule of Siad Barre
summary: Military socialist regime that fought the Ogaden War and fell to clan-based rebellion.

name: Somali Civil War
summary: State collapse, famine, US and UN interventions, Islamist insurgency and al-Shabaab.

name: Republic of Somaliland
summary: Self-declared unrecognised state in the northwest with relative stability and its own institutions.

name: Republic of Djibouti
summary: Former French Somaliland independent in 1977, now host to multiple foreign military bases.

name: Central African Republic
summary: Independent in 1960, ruled briefly as an empire by Bokassa and repeatedly at civil war.

name: Republic of Chad
summary: Sahelian republic independent in 1960, with long civil wars and Libyan intervention.

name: Republic of Cameroon
summary: Former German then French and British territory, independent in 1960-61 and ruled by Paul Biya since 1982.

name: Gabonese Republic
summary: Oil-exporting republic independent in 1960, ruled by the Bongo family from 1967 until a 2023 coup.

name: Republic of Equatorial Guinea
summary: Only Spanish-speaking African state, independent in 1968, oil-rich and highly repressive.

name: Sao Tome and Principe
summary: Atlantic island republic independent from Portugal in 1975.

name: Dutch Cape Colony
summary: VOC settlement at the Cape whose expansion dispossessed Khoikhoi and San and imported slaves.

name: British Cape Colony
summary: British colony that abolished slavery, fought frontier wars and expanded north with diamonds and gold.

name: Zulu Kingdom
summary: State built by Shaka's military revolution, defeated by Britain in 1879 and annexed.

name: Mfecane
summary: Period of upheaval, migration and state formation across southern Africa associated with Zulu expansion.

name: Great Trek
summary: Boer migration inland from the Cape that founded the Transvaal and Orange Free State republics.

name: Anglo-Zulu War
summary: British invasion of Zululand, defeated at Isandlwana before winning at Ulundi.

name: South African Republic and Orange Free State
summary: Boer republics of the Transvaal and Free State, annexed by Britain after the Second Anglo-Boer War.

name: South African Mineral Revolution
summary: Diamond and Witwatersrand gold discoveries that industrialised the region and created migrant labour systems.

name: Second Anglo-Boer War
summary: British conquest of the Boer republics using scorched earth and concentration camps.

name: Union of South Africa
summary: Self-governing dominion uniting four colonies with a whites-only franchise, forerunner of apartheid.

name: Founding of the African National Congress
summary: Formation of the movement that led the struggle against segregation and apartheid.

name: Natives Land Act
summary: Law restricting African land ownership to about 7 percent of the country, the basis of later dispossession.

name: Apartheid
summary: National Party system of racial classification, pass laws, bantustans and forced removals.

name: Sharpeville Massacre
summary: Police killing of 69 anti-pass protesters, after which the ANC and PAC were banned and turned to armed struggle.

name: Republic of South Africa (apartheid era)
summary: Republic that left the Commonwealth in 1961 and faced sanctions, township revolt and regional wars.

name: Rivonia Trial
summary: Trial that sentenced Nelson Mandela and co-accused to life imprisonment.

name: Soweto Uprising
summary: Student protest against Afrikaans instruction met with police fire, igniting a new phase of resistance.

name: South African Negotiated Transition
summary: Mandela's release, unbanning of the ANC and CODESA talks that produced non-racial elections.

name: South African Election of 1994
summary: First universal-franchise election, won by the ANC, making Nelson Mandela president.

name: Republic of South Africa
summary: Constitutional democracy since 1994, with a rights-based constitution and continuing inequality.

name: Presidency of Nelson Mandela
summary: First democratically elected president, who pursued reconciliation and a new constitution.

name: South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission
summary: Tutu-chaired hearings on apartheid-era crimes, offering amnesty for full disclosure.

name: Presidency of Thabo Mbeki
summary: Growth, African Renaissance diplomacy and controversy over HIV/AIDS policy.

name: Presidency of Jacob Zuma
summary: Presidency marked by state capture scandals and economic stagnation, ended by ANC pressure.

name: Presidency of Cyril Ramaphosa
summary: President since 2018, facing energy shortages, corruption inquiries and coalition politics after 2024.

name: German South West Africa
summary: German colony where the Herero and Nama genocide of 1904-08 killed the majority of both peoples.

name: Herero and Nama Genocide
summary: German extermination campaign widely regarded as the twentieth century's first genocide.

name: South West Africa under South African Rule
summary: South African administration that extended apartheid and fought SWAPO's liberation war.

name: Republic of Namibia
summary: Independent in 1990 after a UN-supervised transition following SWAPO's long struggle.

name: Southern Rhodesia
summary: Self-governing British settler colony named for Cecil Rhodes, based on land alienation and white minority rule.

name: Rhodesian Unilateral Declaration of Independence
summary: Ian Smith's white minority government declared independence, triggering sanctions and guerrilla war.

name: Rhodesian Bush War
summary: Liberation war by ZANLA and ZIPRA that forced the Lancaster House settlement.

name: Republic of Zimbabwe
summary: Independent in 1980 under Robert Mugabe, later hit by land seizures and hyperinflation.

name: Rule of Robert Mugabe
summary: Thirty-seven years in power: Gukurahundi massacres, land reform and economic collapse, ended by a coup.

name: Republic of Zambia
summary: Copper-exporting republic independent in 1964 under Kenneth Kaunda.

name: Republic of Malawi
summary: Independent in 1964, ruled for three decades by Hastings Banda before multiparty elections.

name: Republic of Botswana
summary: Diamond-rich republic independent in 1966, one of Africa's most durable democracies.

name: Kingdom of Lesotho
summary: Mountain kingdom founded by Moshoeshoe I, a British protectorate then independent in 1966.

name: Kingdom of Eswatini
summary: Absolute monarchy independent in 1968, renamed from Swaziland in 2018.

name: Republic of Mozambique
summary: Independent from Portugal in 1975 under FRELIMO, then torn by a long civil war.

name: Mozambican Civil War
summary: War between FRELIMO and RENAMO, backed by Rhodesia and South Africa, with about a million deaths.

name: Republic of Angola
summary: Oil-rich state independent from Portugal in 1975, at civil war for most of its first three decades.

name: Angolan Civil War
summary: Cold War proxy war among the MPLA, UNITA and FNLA with Cuban and South African intervention.

name: Kingdom of Madagascar
summary: Merina kingdom that unified most of the island before French conquest.

name: Republic of Madagascar
summary: Indian Ocean island republic independent from France in 1960.

name: Republic of Mauritius
summary: Independent in 1968 and a republic since 1992, with a diversified economy and stable democracy.

name: Republic of Seychelles
summary: Indian Ocean archipelago independent from Britain in 1976.

name: Union of the Comoros
summary: Indian Ocean state independent in 1975, with numerous coups and Mayotte remaining French.

name: Dutch Exploration of New Holland
summary: Dutch navigators charted much of the Australian coast without settling, naming it New Holland.

name: Cook's Voyage to the East Coast of Australia
summary: James Cook charted the east coast and claimed it for Britain at Possession Island.

name: First Fleet
summary: Arrival of eleven ships at Sydney Cove on 26 January 1788 founded the penal colony of New South Wales.

name: Colony of New South Wales
summary: First British colony in Australia, originally a penal settlement covering most of the continent.

name: Convict Transportation to Australia
summary: About 162,000 convicts were transported to Australian colonies over eighty years.

name: Australian Frontier Wars
summary: Sustained violent dispossession of Aboriginal peoples across the continent, with massacres and mass mortality.

name: Colony of Tasmania
summary: Van Diemen's Land separated from New South Wales, notorious for convict settlements and the Black War.

name: Colony of Western Australia
summary: Swan River settlement that later accepted convicts and boomed with 1890s goldfields.

name: Colony of South Australia
summary: Free-settler colony founded on Wakefield's systematic colonisation principles.

name: Colony of Victoria
summary: Separated from New South Wales in 1851 and transformed within a decade by the gold rush.

name: Colony of Queensland
summary: Northern colony separated in 1859, built on pastoralism, sugar and Pacific Islander labour.

name: Australian Gold Rushes
summary: Victorian and New South Wales gold discoveries that tripled the population and reshaped politics.

name: Eureka Stockade
summary: Miners' revolt at Ballarat over licence fees, later mythologised as a birth of Australian democracy.

name: Federation of Australia
summary: Six colonies united as the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January 1901.

name: Commonwealth of Australia
summary: Federal parliamentary monarchy of six states and territories, created by federation in 1901.

name: White Australia Policy
summary: Immigration Restriction Act and successors that excluded non-European migrants for seven decades.

name: ANZAC Landing at Gallipoli
summary: Landing of 25 April 1915 that became the founding national legend of both countries.

name: Stolen Generations
summary: Policies of removing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families.

name: Bombing of Darwin
summary: Japanese air raids on northern Australia that shifted strategic reliance from Britain to the United States.

name: Australian Postwar Immigration Programme
summary: Mass European then global immigration that transformed Australia into a multicultural society.

name: Premiership of Robert Menzies
summary: Australia's longest-serving prime minister, presiding over postwar growth, ANZUS and the Cold War alignment.

name: Australian Referendum of 1967
summary: Over 90 percent voted to allow federal laws for Aboriginal people and their inclusion in the census.

name: Dismissal of the Whitlam Government
summary: Governor-General Kerr dismissed Prime Minister Gough Whitlam, Australia's gravest constitutional crisis.

name: Mabo Decision
summary: High Court ruling recognising native title and rejecting the doctrine of terra nullius.

name: Australian Republic Referendum
summary: Voters rejected replacing the monarchy with a parliamentary-appointed president.

name: Apology to the Stolen Generations
summary: Prime Minister Kevin Rudd's formal parliamentary apology to Indigenous Australians.

name: Indigenous Voice Referendum
summary: Proposal for an Indigenous advisory body in the constitution, rejected by voters.

name: Cook's Circumnavigation of New Zealand
summary: Cook charted both main islands, opening sustained European contact with Maori.

name: Musket Wars
summary: Inter-iwi wars transformed by trade muskets, causing large casualties and migrations before colonisation.

name: Treaty of Waitangi
summary: Agreement between the Crown and Maori chiefs, with differing English and Maori texts, New Zealand's founding document.

name: Colony of New Zealand
summary: British colony that gained self-government in 1852 and fought the New Zealand Wars over land.

name: New Zealand Wars
summary: Conflicts between the Crown, settlers and Maori over sovereignty and land, followed by large confiscations.

name: New Zealand Women's Suffrage
summary: First self-governing country to grant women the parliamentary vote.

name: Dominion of New Zealand
summary: Self-governing dominion from 1907, fully sovereign under the 1947 adoption of the Statute of Westminster.

name: Waitangi Tribunal
summary: Body established to investigate Crown breaches of the Treaty of Waitangi and recommend redress.

name: New Zealand Nuclear-Free Policy
summary: Ban on nuclear-armed and nuclear-powered ships that suspended New Zealand's ANZUS obligations.

name: Kingdom of Hawaii
summary: Kingdom unified by Kamehameha I, overthrown by American settlers in 1893 and annexed in 1898.

name: Kingdom of Tonga
summary: Only Pacific monarchy never formally colonised, a British protected state from 1900 to 1970.

name: Colony of Fiji
summary: British colony whose sugar plantations imported indentured Indian labour, reshaping its society.

name: Republic of Fiji
summary: Independent in 1970 and a republic since 1987, with four coups over ethnic and political disputes.

name: Independence of Samoa
summary: First Pacific island state to gain independence, from New Zealand trusteeship.

name: Independent State of Samoa
summary: Polynesian state independent since 1962, with a fa'amatai chiefly political system.

name: Republic of Nauru
summary: Tiny phosphate island state independent in 1968, later dependent on offshore processing agreements.

name: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
summary: Independent from Australian administration in 1975, the most linguistically diverse country on earth.

name: Bougainville Conflict
summary: Secessionist war over the Panguna mine, ended by peace accords and a 2019 independence referendum.

name: Solomon Islands
summary: Melanesian state independent from Britain in 1978, with ethnic conflict and a regional intervention from 2003.

name: Tuvalu
summary: Polynesian atoll state independent in 1978, among the most exposed to sea-level rise.

name: Republic of Kiribati
summary: Micronesian atoll republic independent from Britain in 1979.

name: Republic of Vanuatu
summary: Independent in 1980 from the Anglo-French New Hebrides condominium.

name: Republic of the Marshall Islands
summary: Freely associated state since 1986, site of US nuclear testing at Bikini and Enewetak.

name: Federated States of Micronesia
summary: Four-state federation in free association with the United States since 1986.

name: Republic of Palau
summary: Last part of the Pacific trust territory to become independent, in free association with the US.

name: Nuclear Testing in the Pacific
summary: American, British and French tests at Bikini, Christmas Island, Maralinga and Mururoa with lasting contamination.

name: French Polynesia
summary: French overseas collectivity of 121 islands, site of nuclear testing at Mururoa.

name: New Caledonia
summary: French territory with a large Kanak population and repeated independence referendums under the Noumea Accord.

name: Pacific Islands Forum
summary: Regional political grouping of Pacific states, prominent in climate diplomacy.

name: Pacific Decolonisation
summary: Successive independences from Samoa in 1962 to Palau in 1994, leaving some territories under metropolitan rule.

name: Age of Discovery
summary: European maritime expansion that linked the hemispheres, founding seaborne empires and global trade routes.

name: Early Modern Period
summary: Era of gunpowder empires, printing, global commerce, scientific revolution and Atlantic slavery.

name: Scientific Revolution
summary: From Copernicus to Newton, the emergence of experimental science and mathematical natural philosophy.

name: Global Silver Trade
summary: American silver flowing via Europe and Manila to China, the first genuinely global commodity circuit.

name: Seventeenth-Century Crisis
summary: Cooling climate, harvest failure, war and rebellion from Europe to China in a century of upheaval.

name: The Enlightenment
summary: Movement of reason, rights and reform whose ideas shaped revolutions and modern constitutions.

name: Industrial Revolution
summary: Mechanised production, steam power and factories that transformed economy, society and population growth.

name: Second Industrial Revolution
summary: Steel, chemicals, electricity, telegraphy and mass production that created the modern industrial economy.

name: Age of Revolutions
summary: Atlantic and European revolutions that spread republicanism, nationalism and abolition.

name: Napoleonic Wars
summary: Global conflict between Napoleonic France and shifting coalitions, fought from Iberia to Russia and at sea.

name: Battle of Trafalgar
summary: Nelson's victory that secured British naval supremacy for a century.

name: Battle of Waterloo
summary: Allied victory in Belgium that ended Napoleon's rule and the Napoleonic Wars.

name: Continental System
summary: Napoleon's blockade of British trade, which damaged European economies and provoked the Peninsular and Russian wars.

name: Congress of Vienna
summary: Great-power settlement that redrew Europe's map, restored monarchies and created a balance of power lasting decades.

name: Concert of Europe
summary: System of great-power consultation and congresses that limited general European war for a century.

name: Revolutions of 1848
summary: Liberal and nationalist uprisings across France, the German states, Italy, Austria and Hungary, mostly defeated.

name: Global Abolition of Slavery
summary: Successive abolitions from revolutionary France and Britain to Brazil that ended legal chattel slavery in the Atlantic world.

name: New Imperialism
summary: Intense European, American and Japanese colonial expansion into Africa, Asia and the Pacific.

name: First Age of Globalisation
summary: Steamships, telegraphs, gold standard and mass migration that integrated the world economy before 1914.

name: First World War
summary: Industrial war among Europe's empires and their allies that killed some 17 million and destroyed four empires.

name: Western Front of the First World War
summary: Four years of trench stalemate in France and Belgium, with battles such as Verdun, the Somme and Passchendaele.

name: Spanish Flu Pandemic
summary: Influenza pandemic that infected a third of humanity and killed an estimated 50 million people.

name: Paris Peace Conference and Treaty of Versailles
summary: Settlement that redrew Europe and the Middle East, imposed reparations on Germany and created the League and mandates.

name: League of Nations
summary: First general international organisation for collective security, weakened by absences and its failures in the 1930s.

name: League of Nations Mandate System
summary: Administration of former German and Ottoman territories by the victors as trusteeships in name.

name: Interwar Period
summary: Two decades of fragile peace: reparations, boom, depression, fascism and the collapse of collective security.

name: Great Depression
summary: Worldwide slump after the 1929 crash, with mass unemployment, deflation, protectionism and political radicalisation.

name: Rise of Fascism
summary: Spread of fascist and authoritarian movements in Italy, Germany, Spain, Japan and beyond between the wars.

name: Second World War
summary: Global war between the Axis and the Allies that killed 70-85 million people and remade the world order.

name: Operation Barbarossa
summary: German invasion of the Soviet Union, the largest land offensive in history and the war's decisive theatre.

name: Battle of Stalingrad
summary: Soviet encirclement and destruction of a German army, the turning point on the Eastern Front.

name: Normandy Landings
summary: Allied invasion of northwest Europe on 6 June 1944 that opened the western front against Germany.

name: The Holocaust
summary: Nazi genocide of about six million Jews, alongside the murder of Roma, disabled people and others.

name: Wannsee Conference
summary: Meeting of German officials to coordinate the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews.

name: Auschwitz-Birkenau
summary: Largest Nazi concentration and extermination camp, where about 1.1 million people were murdered.

name: Genocide Convention
summary: UN convention defining and criminalising genocide, drafted after the Holocaust.

name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
summary: UN General Assembly declaration setting out a common standard of rights for all peoples.

name: Bretton Woods System
summary: Postwar monetary order of fixed exchange rates and dollar-gold convertibility, with the IMF and World Bank.

name: International Monetary Fund
summary: Institution created at Bretton Woods to lend to countries in balance-of-payments difficulty.

name: World Bank
summary: Development lender founded at Bretton Woods, originally for postwar reconstruction.

name: United Nations
summary: Universal international organisation founded in San Francisco in 1945, with 193 member states.

name: United Nations Security Council
summary: Fifteen-member body with five permanent vetoes, responsible for international peace and security.

name: Cold War
summary: Global rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union, fought by proxy, arms race and ideology.

name: Iron Curtain
summary: Division of Europe between Soviet-dominated east and Western-aligned west, symbolised by Churchill's 1946 speech.

name: Truman Doctrine
summary: American commitment to contain communism, beginning with aid to Greece and Turkey.

name: Marshall Plan
summary: American aid programme of about 13 billion dollars that rebuilt Western European economies and tied them together.

name: Comecon
summary: Soviet-led economic organisation coordinating the planned economies of the Eastern bloc.

name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
summary: Transatlantic military alliance founded in 1949 on collective defence under Article 5, now 32 members.

name: Warsaw Pact
summary: Soviet-led military alliance of Eastern bloc states, dissolved in 1991.

name: Nuclear Arms Race
summary: Superpower build-up from the first atomic bombs to tens of thousands of warheads, with deterrence and arms control.

name: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
summary: Treaty limiting the spread of nuclear weapons while recognising five nuclear-weapon states.

name: Decolonisation
summary: Dissolution of the European empires and the emergence of scores of new states across Asia, Africa and the Pacific.

name: Non-Aligned Movement
summary: Grouping of states refusing Cold War alignment, founded at Belgrade after the Bandung Conference.

name: Third World and Global South
summary: Category for states outside the Western and Soviet blocs, later reframed as the Global South.

name: Green Revolution
summary: High-yield crop varieties, fertiliser and irrigation that greatly increased food production in Asia and Latin America.

name: Space Race
summary: Soviet-American competition from Sputnik and Gagarin to Apollo 11 and the Apollo-Soyuz docking.

name: Launch of Sputnik 1
summary: First artificial satellite, launched by the USSR on 4 October 1957, opening the space age.

name: First Human Spaceflight
summary: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth on 12 April 1961 aboard Vostok 1.

name: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
summary: First crewed lunar landing, on 20 July 1969, the culmination of the space race.

name: Detente
summary: Easing of superpower tension with SALT, the Helsinki Accords and expanded trade, ended by Afghanistan.

name: Helsinki Final Act
summary: Agreement recognising postwar borders while committing signatories to human rights, empowering dissidents.

name: Second Cold War
summary: Renewed confrontation after Afghanistan, with missile deployments, SDI and heightened nuclear risk.

name: Revolutions of 1989
summary: Peaceful collapse of communist regimes across Eastern Europe, from Poland to Romania.

name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: Opening of the Wall on 9 November 1989, the emblematic end of Cold War Europe.

name: End of the Cold War
summary: Collapse of the Eastern bloc and dissolution of the USSR, leaving the United States as sole superpower.

name: European Coal and Steel Community
summary: Six-nation pooling of coal and steel, the first step of European integration.

name: Treaty of Rome
summary: Founding treaty of the European Economic Community and Euratom, creating a common market.

name: European Economic Community
summary: Common market of six then twelve states that became the European Union at Maastricht.

name: Schengen Agreement
summary: Agreement abolishing internal border checks, implemented in 1995 and now covering most of the EU.

name: Maastricht Treaty
summary: Treaty creating the European Union, EU citizenship and the path to monetary union.

name: European Union
summary: Union of 27 states with a single market, common currency for most members and supranational institutions.

name: Introduction of the Euro
summary: Single currency launched for accounting in 1999 and as cash in 2002, now used by 20 states.

name: EU Enlargement of 2004
summary: Ten mostly post-communist states joined the European Union, the largest single enlargement.

name: Eurozone Debt Crisis
summary: Sovereign-debt crisis in Greece, Ireland, Portugal, Spain and Cyprus that tested monetary union.

name: European Migrant Crisis
summary: Arrival of over a million asylum seekers, mainly from Syria, straining EU cohesion and border policy.

name: Brexit
summary: Referendum and withdrawal that made the United Kingdom the first state to leave the European Union.

name: Council of Europe
summary: Pan-European human rights body that created the European Convention and its court.

name: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe
summary: Security and human-rights organisation growing out of the Helsinki process.

name: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
summary: Postwar framework of trade negotiation rounds that lowered tariffs worldwide, replaced by the WTO.

name: World Trade Organization
summary: Organisation governing world trade rules and disputes, founded in 1995 from GATT.

name: Contemporary Globalisation
summary: Deepening integration of trade, finance, production and information, with container shipping and the internet.

name: Information Revolution
summary: Microprocessors, personal computing, the internet and mobile networks that reorganised economy and society.

name: World Wide Web
summary: Berners-Lee's invention at CERN that made the internet a mass medium.

name: BRICS
summary: Grouping of major emerging economies, originally Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, later expanded.

name: September 11 Attacks
summary: Al-Qaeda hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and triggered two decades of Western intervention.

name: War on Terror
summary: US-led campaigns after 9/11 in Afghanistan, Iraq and beyond, with drone warfare and expanded surveillance.

name: Global Financial Crisis of 2008
summary: Collapse of the US mortgage market and Lehman Brothers triggered the deepest recession since the 1930s.

name: Great Recession
summary: Worldwide downturn after the financial crisis, with bank rescues, austerity and lasting political effects.

name: Kyoto Protocol
summary: First binding treaty on greenhouse-gas emissions, in force from 2005 without US ratification.

name: Paris Agreement
summary: Universal climate accord committing states to limit warming well below two degrees Celsius.

name: Anthropogenic Climate Change
summary: Industrial-era warming from greenhouse gases, now a central issue of international politics.

name: COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: SARS-CoV-2 pandemic that killed millions, closed borders and economies, and produced vaccines within a year.

name: World Health Organization
summary: UN agency for international health, which coordinated smallpox eradication and pandemic responses.

name: Eradication of Smallpox
summary: WHO campaign that eliminated smallpox, the only human disease so far eradicated.

name: HIV/AIDS Pandemic
summary: Global epidemic that has killed tens of millions, transformed by antiretroviral therapy from the late 1990s.

name: Modern Population Explosion
summary: Growth from about one billion people in 1800 to over eight billion, driven by falling mortality.

name: Age of Mass Migration
summary: Roughly 55 million Europeans and millions of Asians migrated across oceans, reshaping settler societies.

name: International Criminal Court
summary: Permanent court for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity, created by the Rome Statute.

name: Spread of Universal Suffrage
summary: Extension of the vote to women and excluded groups, from New Zealand in 1893 to South Africa in 1994.

name: Rise of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Deep learning and large language models that moved AI into mainstream economic and political consequence.
